questions.stem: Ms. Banks plans a project where students use technology to investigate a local community issue and present recommendations to the city council via a recorded presentation. Using TPACK as a lens, which decision reflects the strongest integration of all three knowledge domains?
options: Selecting a video tool because it allows students to clearly communicate evidence-based civic arguments that align with the content standards and inquiry-based pedagogy
Requiring students to use the tool the teacher personally finds most fun
Avoiding technology entirely so the lesson is simpler to manage
Choosing a presentation tool first and then finding any content that fits it
questions.rationale: Strong TPACK integration aligns the technology with both the content (civic arguments) and pedagogy (inquiry). Choosing a video tool because it serves the content and inquiry goals reflects all three domains working together.

questions.stem: A student who has a physical disability cannot use a standard keyboard and mouse. Which assistive technology consideration is MOST important when planning a technology-rich lesson?
options: Providing alternative input devices, such as switch access or an adapted keyboard, so the student can participate fully
Reducing the lesson's academic rigor for that student
Ensuring the lesson uses only timed activities to build speed
Seating the student away from the technology to avoid frustration
questions.rationale: Assistive technology should provide access. Offering alternative input devices enables a student with a physical disability to participate fully in the technology-rich lesson.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the clearest example of technology used at the Substitution level of SAMR?
options: Students use collaborative software to write a shared document in real time
Students publish their essays to a global audience and receive peer feedback online
Students create a podcast to convey their argument to listeners
Students write an essay using a word processor instead of paper, with no other change in the task
questions.rationale: Substitution is technology acting as a direct tool substitute with no functional change. Typing an essay instead of writing it by hand, with no other change, is Substitution.

questions.stem: Mr. Silva wants to use technology to make his English language learners' content more comprehensible. Which use of technology is MOST appropriate for this goal?
options: Providing dense text-only slides with no visuals or audio support
Removing all visuals so students focus only on the words
Increasing the reading speed of all digital materials
Using multimedia tools that pair text with images, audio narration, and on-demand translation features
questions.rationale: Comprehensible input for English language learners is supported by multiple representations. Pairing text with images, audio, and translation supports access to content.

questions.stem: A district adopts a one-to-one device program. A teacher wants to ensure technology deepens learning rather than merely digitizing worksheets. Which reflective question is MOST useful for guiding her planning?
options: Can I use this tool to reduce the amount of time I spend planning?
Is this the most expensive tool the district purchased?
Does this technology enable students to do something that genuinely deepens or extends their learning beyond what was possible without it?
Does this device make my classroom look more modern to visitors?
questions.rationale: Meaningful integration asks whether technology adds value to learning. Reflecting on whether the tool deepens or extends learning beyond prior possibilities guides purposeful use.

questions.stem: Which of the following best demonstrates teaching students to be critical consumers of digital information?
options: Instructing students to share unverified information quickly so peers stay informed
Telling students that anything found on the internet is reliable
Guiding students to check the author, date, purpose, and corroborating sources before trusting an online claim
Encouraging students to use only the first search result every time
questions.rationale: Critical evaluation of digital information involves examining authorship, currency, purpose, and corroboration. Teaching students to verify these elements builds information literacy.

questions.stem: Ms. Foster wants captions displayed on an instructional video she shows in class. Providing captions is an example of:
options: A feature that lowers academic expectations for the class
A distraction that should generally be avoided
An accessibility feature that supports students who are deaf or hard of hearing and can also benefit many other learners
A practice that benefits only students who are deaf or hard of hearing
questions.rationale: Captions are an accessibility feature reflecting universal design; they support students who are deaf or hard of hearing and benefit many others, such as English learners and students in noisy settings.

questions.stem: Mr. Ito teaches geometry and is deciding whether to add a dynamic geometry software tool to a lesson on transformations. Which justification reflects the MOST appropriate, content-driven reason to integrate the tool?
options: It will keep students busy while he grades other work
The interactive software lets students manipulate figures and immediately observe how transformations change coordinates, deepening conceptual understanding
It allows him to avoid teaching the concept directly
It is the only tool the technology coordinator mentioned this week
questions.rationale: Appropriate integration is driven by how the tool advances the content. Dynamic software that lets students manipulate figures and see transformation effects deepens conceptual understanding of the geometry content.

questions.stem: At the end of a fifth-grade lesson on fractions, Ms. Garcia asks each student to write one problem they solved correctly and one concept that still confuses them, then hand the slip to her as they leave. This strategy is BEST described as:
options: A diagnostic placement test
A summative final exam
An exit ticket used as a formative check for understanding
A standardized benchmark assessment
questions.rationale: An exit ticket is a brief formative assessment collected at the end of a lesson to gauge understanding and inform next steps.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of an effective check for understanding during a lesson?
options: Asking the whole class, 'Does everyone understand?' and continuing when no one objects
Calling only on students who always raise their hands
Waiting until the unit test to find out who learned the material
Having all students respond on individual whiteboards to a question so the teacher can quickly see each student's thinking
questions.rationale: Effective checks for understanding elicit a response from every student so the teacher can gauge whole-class understanding. Individual whiteboard responses make all students' thinking visible.

questions.stem: After grading a formative quiz, Mr. Lambert finds that most of his class mastered the objective but six students share the same misconception. Which response best reflects data-driven instructional decision making?
options: Assign the six students extra homework with no additional instruction
Move on to the next unit because most students did well
Pull the six students into a small group for targeted reteaching while others extend their learning
Reteach the entire concept to the whole class from the beginning
questions.rationale: Data-driven decisions use assessment results to differentiate. Targeted small-group reteaching for the six students addresses their specific need while others move forward.

questions.stem: During independent work, Mr. Reyes circulates and notices several students making the same error in solving two-step equations. What is the BEST immediate next step?
options: Lower the grades of the students who made the error
Pause the class briefly to address the common error and model the correct process, then have students continue
Wait until the next day to address the error so as not to interrupt work time
Tell the students to look up the answer themselves
questions.rationale: Monitoring during instruction allows real-time responsiveness. Pausing to address a common error and model the correct process corrects the misunderstanding before it becomes ingrained.

questions.stem: A teacher analyzes a class's results on a constructed-response item and finds that students who scored low all struggled to identify the main idea, while students who scored high did not. The MOST instructionally sound interpretation is that the teacher should:
options: Give every student the same whole-class lesson again regardless of the pattern
Conclude the test was poorly written and discard the data
Use the pattern to plan focused instruction on identifying main ideas for the students who need it
Assume the low-scoring students simply did not try
questions.rationale: Disaggregating data reveals specific skill gaps. The pattern points to a need for focused instruction on main idea for the students who struggled, a targeted, data-driven decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes flexible grouping?
options: Grouping students only by where they sit in the classroom
Always letting students choose their own friends as group members
Permanently assigning students to fixed ability levels for the entire year
Forming and re-forming groups based on students' current needs, the task, and ongoing assessment data
questions.rationale: Flexible grouping forms temporary groups that change based on the task, students' current needs, and assessment data, avoiding permanent labels.

questions.stem: Each of the following is a feature of high-quality feedback EXCEPT:
options: It focuses only on assigning a number or letter grade with no guidance
It tells the student what was done well and what to improve next
It is specific and tied to the learning goal
It is timely enough for the student to act on it
questions.rationale: High-quality feedback is specific, timely, goal-referenced, and actionable. A grade alone with no guidance does not help the student improve.

questions.stem: Ms. Quintero gives a brief mid-unit assessment and uses the results to sort students into temporary groups: one reviewing prerequisite skills, one practicing the current standard, and one working on an enrichment extension. Two weeks later she reassesses and re-forms the groups. This practice BEST demonstrates:
options: Using assessment data to drive responsive, flexible grouping that changes as students progress
Eliminating the need for any further assessment
Tracking students permanently by ability
Grouping students randomly to save planning time
questions.rationale: Reassessing and re-forming groups based on current data exemplifies data-driven flexible grouping that responds to student progress over time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the LEAST effective approach to monitoring student understanding during a lesson?
options: Assuming students understand because the room is quiet and no one asks questions
Collecting brief written responses partway through the lesson
Using cold-call questioning that gives every student a chance to be asked
Circulating to observe student work and listen to student discussions
questions.rationale: Effective monitoring gathers evidence from all students. Assuming understanding from quiet compliance provides no actual evidence of learning.

questions.stem: Ms. Castillo has used several formative assessments and notices that one student consistently demonstrates mastery quickly and shows signs of boredom. The MOST appropriate data-driven response is to:
options: Reduce the student's grade for finishing too quickly
Provide an appropriately challenging extension or enrichment task aligned to the standard
Give the student more of the same practice problems to fill the time
Ask the student to wait quietly until the rest of the class finishes
questions.rationale: Data-driven differentiation responds to advanced learners by offering appropriately challenging extensions that keep them engaged and learning, not idle repetition.

questions.stem: Ms. Howard collects formative data over a week and creates a simple chart showing each student's progress toward the unit's key skills. Which use of this data best reflects sound, data-driven instructional decision making?
options: Assigning final unit grades based solely on the first day's data
Using the chart to identify which students need reteaching, which are ready to advance, and how to form responsive groups
Sharing each student's ranked scores publicly to motivate the class
Filing the chart away to show during her annual evaluation only
questions.rationale: Sound data-driven decision making uses progress data to differentiate, identifying who needs reteaching, who is ready to advance, and how to group students responsively.

questions.stem: Ms. Alvarado wants to build a strong partnership with the families in her third-grade class at the start of the year. Which of the following is the most effective first step toward that goal?
options: Asking families to sign a contract committing to a set number of volunteer hours
Waiting until the first scheduled conference to make personal contact with each family
Reaching out with a warm welcome message that invites families to share their hopes and information about their child
Sending home a detailed list of classroom rules and the consequences for breaking them
questions.rationale: Effective family partnerships begin with positive, two-way communication that conveys welcome and invites families to share their knowledge of and goals for their child. This establishes trust and positions families as valued partners from the outset.

questions.stem: Mr. Boateng is preparing for his first parent-teacher conference of the year with the family of a student who is doing well academically. Which approach best reflects effective conference practice?
options: Beginning with the student's strengths and progress, then discussing goals collaboratively
Presenting only the student's test scores and percentile rankings
Telling the family exactly what they must do at home to keep the student on track
Focusing the entire conversation on areas where the student could still improve
questions.rationale: Effective conferences open on a positive note by highlighting strengths and progress, then move into collaborative goal-setting. This builds rapport and keeps families engaged as partners rather than recipients of directives.

questions.stem: Several families in Ms. Castellano's class are recent immigrants whose home language is not English. To communicate effectively and respectfully with these families, the teacher should do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Arrange for qualified interpreters or translated materials when needed
Assume that limited English proficiency reflects limited interest in their child's education
Provide multiple ways for families to engage, including flexible meeting times
Learn about the cultural backgrounds and communication norms of the families
questions.rationale: Culturally responsive engagement requires recognizing that language barriers are not interest barriers. Assuming low English proficiency signals low investment is a deficit-based stereotype that damages partnerships; the other options support genuine access and respect.

questions.stem: In a co-teaching classroom, Ms. Dunn (general educator) and Mr. Patel (special educator) decide that one will lead a lesson while the other circulates to monitor understanding, provide cues, and collect informal data. Which co-teaching model are they using?
options: One teach, one observe/assist
Parallel teaching
Team teaching
Station teaching
questions.rationale: In the 'one teach, one observe/assist' model, one teacher delivers instruction while the other monitors students, offers support, and gathers data. This matches the described division of roles.

questions.stem: A first-year teacher, Mr. Okonkwo, is paired with an experienced mentor. Which interaction would most clearly reflect the intended purpose of an effective mentoring relationship?
options: The mentor completes the new teacher's lesson plans so they meet district standards
The mentor advises the new teacher to avoid asking questions that might appear inexperienced
The mentor observes a lesson and then engages the new teacher in reflective questioning about instructional decisions
The mentor reports the new teacher's weaknesses directly to the principal for evaluation
questions.rationale: Effective mentoring promotes the new teacher's growth and self-reflection. Observing followed by reflective, non-evaluative questioning helps the mentee analyze and improve their own practice rather than fostering dependence or fear.

questions.stem: After teaching a unit, Ms. Reyes reviews her assessment results and notes that students struggled with a concept she thought she had taught clearly. According to the principle of reflective practice, what is the most appropriate next step?
options: Move on to the next unit to stay on the district pacing calendar
Conclude that the students simply did not study hard enough
Lower the difficulty of the next test so scores improve
Examine her instructional choices to identify what to adjust before reteaching
questions.rationale: Reflective practice involves analyzing one's own teaching to understand and improve student outcomes. The teacher should examine her instructional decisions to identify adjustments, rather than blaming students or masking the problem.

questions.stem: Mr. Lindqvist regularly sends home a class newsletter and posts updates online, yet several families rarely respond or attend events. Which interpretation best reflects a culturally responsive understanding of this situation?
options: The teacher's current outreach methods may not align with how all families prefer or are able to engage
The school should reduce its outreach efforts to avoid wasting resources
These families are not invested in their children's education
Family engagement is impossible to achieve with these families
questions.rationale: Culturally responsive practice attributes low participation to barriers and mismatched outreach methods rather than to family deficits. The teacher should consider varied communication channels, languages, schedules, and definitions of involvement.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes two-way communication between a teacher and families?
options: A monthly newsletter that informs families of upcoming events
An exchange in which both the teacher and families share information and respond to one another
A grade report posted to the online portal each grading period
A flyer announcing the date of the school open house
questions.rationale: Two-way communication is reciprocal: information flows in both directions, with families and teachers contributing and responding. The other options are one-way (teacher-to-family) communications.

questions.stem: A speech-language pathologist will begin working with a student in Ms. Nakamura's class. To collaborate effectively with this specialist, Ms. Nakamura should first:
options: Share relevant classroom observations and coordinate how supports will be reinforced in class
Wait for the specialist to request information before offering any
Hand over full responsibility for the student's communication goals to the specialist
Limit the specialist's involvement to pull-out sessions outside the classroom
questions.rationale: Effective collaboration with specialists is reciprocal and proactive. The teacher should share classroom observations and coordinate how strategies will be reinforced in the general setting so that supports are consistent and integrated.

questions.stem: During a PLC meeting, data show that English learners across all sections are underperforming on a recent writing assessment. One colleague suggests simply giving these students easier prompts. As a reflective, collaborative professional, which response best advances the PLC's purpose?
options: Agreeing to lower expectations so the students' scores will rise
Proposing that the team examine the writing supports and scaffolds being used and share strategies that have worked
Concluding that the assessment is unfair and should be discarded
Recommending the students be removed from the writing assessment entirely
questions.rationale: A PLC's purpose is to use data to improve instruction while maintaining high expectations. Investigating the scaffolds in use and sharing effective strategies maintains rigor and targets the instructional response to the identified need.

questions.stem: A teacher chooses to attend a workshop on strategies for supporting students with dyslexia because several of her students have this diagnosis. This decision best illustrates which professional responsibility?
options: Avoiding collaboration with colleagues
Engaging in professional development aligned with student needs
Fulfilling a mandatory state testing requirement
Reducing her instructional planning time
questions.rationale: Selecting professional development based on the specific needs of one's students reflects purposeful, ongoing professional growth—a core professional responsibility for improving instruction.

questions.stem: Ms. Farouk plans a 'family math night' but notices that mostly the same few families attend her events while many others never do. To make her family engagement efforts more equitable, which strategy would be LEAST effective?
options: Providing childcare and food to remove participation barriers
Offering events at varied times, including some virtual options
Asking families directly about the times, formats, and topics that would draw them in
Continuing to use only the same English-language flyer to advertise events
questions.rationale: Equitable engagement requires reducing barriers and adapting outreach. Repeating a single English flyer ignores language and access barriers and is the least effective strategy; the others actively remove barriers and invite family input.

questions.stem: Two co-teachers want to divide the class into three groups, each completing a different portion of the lesson content before students rotate through all three. Which co-teaching model are they planning to use?
options: Station teaching
One teach, one assist
Parallel teaching
Alternative teaching
questions.rationale: Station teaching divides content into stations through which students rotate, with teachers stationed at points of instruction. Dividing content into rotating groups is the defining feature of this model.

questions.stem: A veteran teacher, Mr. Delacroix, privately disagrees with a new schoolwide instructional initiative he believes lacks research support. Which course of action best reflects professional advocacy and collegial ethics?
options: Publicly criticizing the initiative in front of students and parents
Ignoring the initiative entirely and continuing his own methods without comment
Raising his evidence-based concerns through appropriate professional channels while remaining open to dialogue
Refusing to implement the initiative and encouraging colleagues to do the same
questions.rationale: Professional advocacy means voicing concerns constructively through appropriate channels, supported by evidence, while remaining collaborative. This respects collegial relationships and the change process without undermining the school community.

questions.stem: Which of the following communications is most likely to strengthen a teacher's relationship with a family?
options: A form letter sent to all families with the student's name inserted
An email sent only after a problem has become serious
A note recognizing a specific positive thing the student did that week
A phone call home only when the student misbehaves
questions.rationale: Proactive positive communication—such as a personalized note recognizing a specific accomplishment—builds trust and goodwill, strengthening the partnership and making later problem-solving conversations more productive.

questions.stem: Ms. Whitfield keeps a journal in which, after each unit, she records what worked, what did not, and what she will change. Over time she uses these notes to refine her teaching. This practice most directly supports:
options: Documentation needed for parent conferences
Preparation for the annual standardized assessment
Continuous improvement of instruction through systematic reflection
Compliance with the district's lesson plan submission policy
questions.rationale: Maintaining and using a reflective journal to analyze and adjust teaching is a hallmark of reflective practice that drives continuous instructional improvement over time.

questions.stem: A family informs Mr. Yusuf that, in their culture, making direct eye contact with an adult authority figure can be considered disrespectful. How should this information best influence the teacher's practice?
options: He should recognize the cultural meaning of the behavior and avoid misreading it
He should require the student to make eye contact to build confidence
He should report the family's belief to administration as a concern
He should interpret the student's averted gaze as a sign of dishonesty
questions.rationale: Culturally responsive teaching requires understanding that communication norms vary across cultures. The teacher should honor this knowledge, avoid misinterpreting averted eye contact, and adjust expectations accordingly.

questions.stem: A grade-level team is forming norms for their new PLC. Which proposed norm would LEAST support the PLC's effectiveness?
options: The team will hold itself accountable for following through on agreed actions
Disagreements about data interpretation should be avoided to keep meetings pleasant
Decisions about instruction should be grounded in student data
Each member's perspective will be heard and respected
questions.rationale: Productive PLCs welcome professional disagreement as a path to deeper analysis. A norm that suppresses disagreement to preserve comfort undermines rigorous inquiry; the other norms support data use, respect, and accountability.

questions.stem: Before an annual review meeting for a student receiving special education services, the family will participate as members of the team. Which teacher action best supports meaningful family participation?
options: Limiting the family's role to signing the required forms
Using technical jargon to convey the teacher's expertise
Presenting conclusions that have already been finalized by the staff
Sending the family information in advance and inviting their input and questions
questions.rationale: Meaningful participation requires that families have access to information beforehand and genuine opportunities to contribute. Sharing materials in advance and inviting input positions families as equal team members.

questions.stem: In a co-teaching pair, one teacher notices that students who need reteaching of a foundational skill are being pulled into a small group, while the other teacher continues the lesson with the rest of the class. Which co-teaching model is being used?
options: Station teaching
Parallel teaching
Team teaching
Alternative teaching
questions.rationale: Alternative teaching involves one teacher working with a small group—often for reteaching, preteaching, or enrichment—while the other teaches the larger group. The described scenario matches this model.

questions.stem: Which of the following best demonstrates a teacher advocating for students' needs?
options: Requesting additional resources and supports for students who are struggling to access the curriculum
Lowering academic standards so that more students pass
Avoiding conversations with administrators about classroom challenges
Keeping concerns about inadequate materials to oneself
questions.rationale: Advocacy means actively working to secure the conditions and resources students need to succeed. Requesting additional supports for struggling students exemplifies advocacy on their behalf.

questions.stem: Mr. Ibarra wants families to view themselves as partners in their children's learning rather than as passive recipients of school decisions. Which long-term strategy best supports this vision of family engagement?
options: Increasing the number of one-way newsletters sent home each month
Inviting families to share their goals, culture, and knowledge and incorporating their input into classroom decisions
Creating a detailed handbook of rules families are expected to enforce at home
Scheduling more events where the school presents information to families
questions.rationale: Positioning families as partners requires reciprocal engagement that values their knowledge and incorporates their voice into decisions. This shared ownership distinguishes partnership from one-way, school-directed communication.

questions.stem: A new teacher seeks feedback from a trusted colleague after a difficult lesson. The colleague responds, 'What did you notice about how students responded, and what might you try differently?' This response best reflects:
options: A coaching stance that prompts reflection and self-directed problem-solving
An evaluative judgment of the teacher's competence
An attempt to avoid the conversation
A refusal to provide direct help
questions.rationale: Open, reflective questioning is characteristic of a coaching stance that helps a colleague analyze their own practice and generate solutions, building professional capacity rather than issuing judgments.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to keep families regularly informed about classroom learning in a way that is accessible to families with varied schedules and resources. Which approach is most effective?
options: Relying solely on a printed flyer posted on the classroom door
Offering multiple communication channels, such as texts, emails, and a translated class app
Posting updates only on a personal social media account
Communicating only during the two scheduled conference weeks
questions.rationale: Because families differ in access and preferences, offering multiple communication channels—including translation—maximizes reach and ensures more families can stay informed and engaged.

questions.stem: A counselor shares with Ms. Adeyemi confidential information about a student's home situation that explains recent behavior changes. Which response best balances collaboration with professional ethics?
options: Mentioning it casually to the student so they know the teacher understands
Using the information privately to provide sensitive, appropriate support while keeping it confidential
Sharing the information with the rest of the grade-level team so everyone is aware
Recording the details in a shared online document for future reference
questions.rationale: Effective collaboration with specialists must respect confidentiality. The teacher should use the information privately to inform compassionate support while protecting the student's and family's privacy, sharing only on a legitimate need-to-know basis.

questions.stem: During collaborative planning, two co-teachers disagree about how to pace an upcoming unit. Which approach best reflects effective professional collaboration?
options: Deferring entirely to whichever teacher has more years of experience
Having each teacher quietly pace the unit their own way
Splitting the difference without examining the instructional implications
Discussing each other's reasoning and using student needs and data to reach a shared decision
questions.rationale: Effective collaboration resolves differences through professional dialogue grounded in student needs and data, leading to a shared, well-reasoned decision rather than deference to seniority or unexamined compromise.

questions.stem: A teacher is documenting a student's progress to share with the family at an upcoming conference. Which collection of evidence would be most useful for a productive, partnership-oriented conversation?
options: A single anecdote about a behavior incident
Only the student's lowest test scores to emphasize the need for improvement
A balanced set of work samples, observations, and assessment results showing growth and next steps
The student's ranking compared to classmates
questions.rationale: A productive conference draws on varied, balanced evidence—work samples, observations, and assessments—that shows growth and identifies next steps, giving families a complete picture and a basis for collaboration.

questions.stem: A school forms vertical teams in which teachers from consecutive grade levels meet to align curriculum. The primary benefit of this collaboration is that it:
options: Reduces the number of meetings teachers must attend
Eliminates the need for individual lesson planning
Allows teachers to avoid teaching difficult standards
Promotes continuity and smooth transitions in student learning across grade levels
questions.rationale: Vertical teaming connects teachers across grade levels to align instruction, ensuring coherence and smoother transitions so that learning builds logically from one grade to the next.

questions.stem: Ms. Petrov suspects that her own assumptions about a particular family may be affecting how she communicates with them. As a reflective and culturally responsive professional, what should she do first?
options: Avoid contact with the family to prevent any conflict
Ask other teachers whether they share her negative view of the family
Limit communication to required notices only
Examine her own biases and assumptions and consider how they shape her interactions
questions.rationale: Culturally responsive practice requires educators to reflect on and confront their own biases. Self-examination of assumptions is the necessary first step toward more equitable, respectful communication.

questions.stem: A teacher returns from a district professional development session on a new formative assessment strategy. Which action best ensures the PD has a lasting impact on student learning?
options: Sharing only that the session was interesting with colleagues
Filing the session handouts for possible future reference
Implementing the strategy, reflecting on its effects, and adjusting based on student results
Waiting until next year to consider trying the strategy
questions.rationale: Professional development translates into impact when teachers apply new strategies, reflect on their effects, and refine practice based on student outcomes. This cycle of application and reflection produces lasting improvement.

questions.stem: A parent emails a teacher expressing frustration that they did not learn about their child's failing grades until report cards were issued. Reflecting on this feedback, what change should the teacher prioritize?
options: Establishing regular, proactive communication so families are informed of concerns early
Reducing the amount of feedback given on assignments
Asking the parent to check the online portal more frequently
Defending the timing by noting that report cards are issued on schedule
questions.rationale: The feedback signals a gap in proactive communication. Prioritizing regular, early updates about academic concerns prevents surprises and supports timely collaboration with families.

questions.stem: A campus is implementing inclusion, and a general educator will share students and planning time with a special educator for the first time. To establish an effective co-teaching partnership, which step should the pair address EARLIEST?
options: Deciding which teacher will handle all discipline issues
Clarifying shared roles, responsibilities, and expectations for both instruction and classroom management
Determining how to divide grading paperwork between them
Choosing which co-teaching model to use for the entire year
questions.rationale: A successful co-teaching partnership begins by jointly clarifying roles, responsibilities, and expectations for instruction and management. This shared foundation of parity and communication guides all later decisions about models and logistics.

questions.stem: Ms. Alvarez, a fourth-grade teacher, notices unexplained bruises on a student and suspects the child may be a victim of abuse. According to Texas law, what is her PRIMARY legal obligation?
options: She must personally report the suspected abuse, even if she also tells the principal.
She must report the suspicion only if another colleague agrees with her assessment.
She must first contact the child's parents to ask about the bruises before reporting.
She must wait until she has gathered conclusive proof before taking any action.
questions.rationale: Under Texas law, any professional who suspects child abuse has a personal, non-delegable duty to report directly to the appropriate authorities. Telling a supervisor does not satisfy this obligation.

questions.stem: A parent calls Ms. Chen and asks her to share the test grades of her daughter's classmate, claiming the two students are competing for a scholarship. Under FERPA, what is Ms. Chen's MOST appropriate response?
options: Decline, because a classmate's education records may not be disclosed to another parent without consent.
Provide the grades, since the parent has a legitimate scholarship-related reason.
Refer the parent to the competing student's parent to obtain the grades directly.
Provide only the numerical scores but withhold the classmate's name.
questions.rationale: FERPA protects students' education records from disclosure to unauthorized parties. A parent has rights only to their own child's records, not to another student's grades, absent consent.

questions.stem: During an ARD committee meeting, the participants are determining the educational placement for a student with a disability. Which principle requires that the student be educated with non-disabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate?
options: Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE)
Procedural due process
Prior written notice
Least Restrictive Environment (LRE)
questions.rationale: The Least Restrictive Environment principle under IDEA requires that students with disabilities be educated alongside non-disabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate to their needs.

questions.stem: Mr. Delgado wants to use a 30-second clip from a popular film and a single chapter from a novel to enhance his lesson on theme. He plans to use the materials only for face-to-face teaching in his classroom. Which doctrine MOST directly supports his limited educational use?
options: Public domain
First-sale doctrine
Creative Commons licensing
Fair use
questions.rationale: Fair use permits limited use of copyrighted material for purposes such as teaching, considering factors like purpose, amount used, and effect on the market. A brief clip and a single chapter for instruction generally fall within fair use.

questions.stem: A high school teacher receives a friend request on a personal social media account from a current student. Considering professional boundaries and the Texas Educators' Code of Ethics, which response is MOST appropriate?
options: Accept the request to build rapport, since the platform is public anyway.
Accept the request but ask the student to keep the connection confidential.
Decline the request and, if needed, communicate with the student only through district-approved channels.
Accept the request but adjust privacy settings so the student sees limited content.
questions.rationale: To maintain appropriate professional boundaries, educators should avoid private social media connections with current students and communicate only through district-sanctioned channels, protecting both the student and the teacher.

questions.stem: A student who does not qualify for special education under IDEA has a documented medical condition that substantially limits a major life activity. Under which law is the student MOST likely to receive accommodations through a written plan?
options: The Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA)
The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA)
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act
The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)
questions.rationale: Section 504 provides accommodations for students with a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits a major life activity but who do not require specialized instruction under IDEA. The plan is commonly called a 504 plan.

questions.stem: Which document is developed by the ARD committee and contains a student's annual goals, services, accommodations, and present levels of academic and functional performance?
options: An Individualized Education Program (IEP)
A 504 accommodation plan
A response-to-intervention log
A behavior intervention summary
questions.rationale: The Individualized Education Program (IEP) is developed by the ARD committee for a student receiving special education services and includes goals, services, accommodations, and present levels of performance.

questions.stem: Mr. Han disagrees with the special education services proposed by the school and believes his son needs additional support. The school and parent cannot reach agreement. Which procedural safeguard allows Mr. Han to formally challenge the decision before an impartial hearing officer?
options: A due process hearing
A manifestation determination
An eligibility re-evaluation
A functional behavior assessment
questions.rationale: A due process hearing is a procedural safeguard under IDEA that allows parents to formally dispute decisions about identification, evaluation, placement, or services before an impartial hearing officer.

questions.stem: A district adopts an Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) for student technology. What is the PRIMARY purpose of such a policy?
options: To define appropriate, responsible use of district technology and online resources
To grant students unrestricted access to all internet content
To increase the school's revenue from technology vendors
To eliminate the need for teacher supervision during computer use
questions.rationale: An Acceptable Use Policy establishes expectations for the responsible, appropriate, and safe use of district technology and online resources by students and staff.

questions.stem: Ms. Ibarra teaches an online course and wants to display copyrighted materials to enrolled students through the district's learning management system. Which law specifically addresses the use of copyrighted works in accredited, mediated distance education?
options: The first-sale doctrine
The Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA)
The Children's Internet Protection Act (CIPA)
The TEACH Act
questions.rationale: The TEACH Act (Technology, Education, and Copyright Harmonization Act) governs the use of copyrighted materials in accredited, mediated distance education delivered through secure systems to enrolled students.

questions.stem: During recess duty, Mr. Jackson is responsible for supervising 60 students on the playground. To best fulfill his duty of safe supervision, what should he do?
options: Position himself where he can grade papers while seated against the wall
Actively circulate and maintain clear sightlines across the entire play area
Focus his attention solely on the students he personally teaches
Allow students to police themselves while he steps inside to make copies
questions.rationale: Safe supervision requires educators to be actively engaged, mobile, and positioned to observe all students, allowing them to anticipate and respond to hazards promptly.

questions.stem: Under FERPA, which of the following is generally considered 'directory information' that a school MAY disclose without prior consent, provided parents were given the opportunity to opt out?
options: A student's disciplinary records
A student's Social Security number
A student's name and participation in officially recognized activities
A student's special education eligibility status
questions.rationale: Directory information can include items such as a student's name, photograph, and participation in officially recognized activities, which a school may disclose after providing notice and an opt-out opportunity.

questions.stem: What does the acronym 'ARD' stand for in the Texas special education process?
options: Academic Resource Development
Annual Review of Disabilities
Admission, Review, and Dismissal
Assessment, Referral, and Determination
questions.rationale: In Texas, ARD stands for Admission, Review, and Dismissal. The ARD committee makes decisions about a student's special education identification, services, and placement.

questions.stem: A student with a disability is suspended for a behavior incident. Before the suspension can extend beyond the threshold that constitutes a change in placement, the school must convene a meeting to determine whether the behavior was a result of the student's disability. This meeting is called a:
options: Functional behavior assessment
Manifestation determination review
Prior written notice conference
Least restrictive environment review
questions.rationale: A manifestation determination review examines whether a student's misconduct was caused by, or directly related to, the disability, or resulted from the school's failure to implement the IEP. It is required when disciplinary removals constitute a change in placement.

questions.stem: Ms. Kowalski wants to ensure her communication with a parent about a student's progress complies with confidentiality expectations. Which practice is LEAST appropriate?
options: Sending sensitive progress details to the parent's verified email address
Discussing the student's confidential information with a colleague who has no instructional role with the student
Discussing the student's grades in a private conference with the parent
Documenting communications and storing them securely
questions.rationale: Confidential student information should be shared only with those who have a legitimate educational interest. Discussing it with a colleague who has no instructional relationship with the student violates confidentiality.

questions.stem: The guarantee that a student with a disability receives special education and related services at no cost to the parents and tailored to the student's individual needs is known as:
options: Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE)
Least Restrictive Environment (LRE)
Response to Intervention (RTI)
Acceptable Use Policy (AUP)
questions.rationale: Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE) under IDEA guarantees that eligible students receive special education and related services at no cost, designed to meet their individual needs.

questions.stem: Mr. Nakamura, a coach, frequently texts individual athletes late at night about non-team matters and offers to drive them home alone. From an ethical and professional-boundaries standpoint, the MOST significant concern is that these behaviors:
options: Are acceptable as long as the parents are unaware
Improve team performance and should be encouraged
Demonstrate strong commitment and mentorship without any concern
Create an inappropriate, private relationship that erodes professional boundaries
questions.rationale: Late-night private texting about non-team matters and one-on-one transportation create inappropriate private relationships and blur professional boundaries, posing risks to students and violating ethical expectations.

questions.stem: A teacher new to Texas wants to understand the source of the standards governing professional conduct, ethical practices, and discipline of educators. Which entity adopts the Texas Educators' Code of Ethics?
options: The regional Education Service Center board
The local campus site-based decision-making committee
The United States Department of Education
The State Board for Educator Certification (SBEC)
questions.rationale: The State Board for Educator Certification (SBEC) adopts and enforces the Texas Educators' Code of Ethics, which governs professional conduct and ethical practices for Texas educators.

questions.stem: Ms. Ortega finds a high-quality worksheet online and wants to make copies for her class. The website states 'All rights reserved' and requires payment for classroom licenses. Which action is MOST consistent with copyright law?
options: Copy the worksheet freely because it is for educational use
Share the file with colleagues so each can copy it independently
Purchase the appropriate license or obtain permission before copying
Remove the copyright notice and then distribute the copies
questions.rationale: When a work is clearly copyrighted with rights reserved and a license is required, the educator should purchase the license or obtain permission. Educational use does not automatically override explicit licensing requirements.

questions.stem: A parent submits a written request to inspect and review their child's education records. Under FERPA, the school must generally comply within what reasonable time frame?
options: No more than 45 days
Only after the end of the school year
Only if the principal personally approves
No more than 6 months
questions.rationale: FERPA requires schools to provide parents access to inspect and review their child's education records within a reasonable time, not to exceed 45 days after the request is made.

questions.stem: A required member of an ARD committee for a Texas student typically includes all of the following EXCEPT:
options: A general education teacher of the student
A representative of the school district qualified to provide or supervise special education
A randomly selected parent from another student's family
The student's parent or guardian
questions.rationale: Required ARD committee members include the parent, a general education teacher, a special education teacher, and a district representative qualified in special education. An unrelated parent from another family is not a required or appropriate member.

questions.stem: Mr. Park suspects neglect after a student repeatedly arrives hungry and in unwashed clothing. A colleague tells him, 'Don't worry, I'll let the counselor know.' What is Mr. Park's MOST appropriate next step?
options: Wait several weeks to confirm a pattern before deciding whether to report
Document the concern privately but take no further action unless asked
Rely on the colleague to handle the report since the counselor will be informed
Make his own report to the appropriate authorities within the required time frame
questions.rationale: The duty to report suspected abuse or neglect is personal and non-delegable. Mr. Park must make his own report to the proper authorities within the legally required time frame, regardless of what a colleague says they will do.

questions.stem: A teacher posts on a personal, public social media account a photo of her class taken during a field trip, tagging several students by name and noting their behavior. Which concern is MOST relevant?
options: The post is fine as long as the school's name is not mentioned
The post is acceptable because field trips are public events
The post is only a problem if a parent complains directly
The post could violate student privacy and professional-boundary expectations
questions.rationale: Posting identifiable students with names and behavioral commentary on a personal public account can violate student privacy and professional-boundary expectations, regardless of consent status or complaints.

questions.stem: An ARD committee is choosing a placement for a student with a learning disability. The committee considers, in order, a continuum ranging from the general education classroom with supports to a fully separate setting. Which approach BEST reflects the LRE requirement?
options: Choose the most restrictive setting to avoid future placement changes
Place the student in whichever setting has the most available seats
Automatically place the student in a self-contained classroom to maximize support
Begin by considering the general education setting with appropriate aids and services, moving to more restrictive options only as needed
questions.rationale: The LRE requirement obligates the committee to first consider the general education environment with supplementary aids and services, moving to more restrictive placements only when the student's needs cannot be met in less restrictive settings.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a teacher's ethical responsibility regarding accepting gifts from students or parents?
options: Teachers must accept gifts only during the holiday season
Teachers should accept all expensive gifts to avoid offending families
Teachers should be cautious about accepting gifts that could appear to improperly influence professional judgment
Teachers may solicit gifts in exchange for higher grades
questions.rationale: The code of ethics cautions educators against accepting gifts that could reasonably appear to influence professional decisions or judgment. Token gestures may be acceptable, but anything that could compromise objectivity should be avoided.

questions.stem: Ms. Quintero is asked by a counselor from another school district to share a transferring student's records. The new district enrolls the student and requests the records to support the student's education. Under FERPA, this disclosure is:
options: Prohibited unless the parent first sues for access
Generally permitted to officials of a school where the student seeks or intends to enroll
Allowed only if the records are at least five years old
Permitted only if the student is over 18 years old
questions.rationale: FERPA permits disclosure of education records, without prior consent, to officials of another school or district in which the student seeks or intends to enroll. This supports continuity of the student's education.

questions.stem: A teacher applies the four factors of fair use to decide whether copying material is permissible. Which scenario is LEAST likely to be considered fair use?
options: Displaying a single image to illustrate a concept during a lesson
Copying an entire workbook designed to be consumed for classroom use
Quoting a short excerpt from an article for student analysis
Using a brief passage from a poem for critique in class
questions.rationale: Copying an entire consumable workbook, which is designed to be purchased and used up, undermines the market for the work and uses the whole work, making it least likely to qualify as fair use.

questions.stem: During a field trip, Mr. Reyes is responsible for a group of students. To best ensure safe supervision in this less-controlled environment, he should:
options: Maintain an appropriate supervision ratio, conduct frequent head counts, and keep students within sight
Focus only on responding to problems after they occur
Allow students to explore individually and reconvene at the end of the day
Assign one responsible student to monitor the rest of the group
questions.rationale: Safe supervision on field trips requires maintaining appropriate adult-to-student ratios, conducting regular head counts, and keeping students within sight to anticipate and prevent hazards in unfamiliar settings.

questions.stem: A Texas school district must, by law, establish a program to identify and provide services for students who exhibit characteristics of dyslexia. Which action by a teacher BEST supports the district's obligation?
options: Recognizing early warning signs and referring students for appropriate screening and evaluation
Telling parents their child will simply outgrow reading difficulties
Waiting until secondary school before any intervention is considered
Discouraging referrals to avoid overidentifying students
questions.rationale: Teachers support the district's legal obligation by recognizing early indicators of dyslexia and referring students for appropriate screening and evaluation so that timely, effective services can be provided.

questions.stem: Ms. Alvarado teaches a third-grade class in which most students can decode multisyllabic words accurately but struggle to summarize what they read. Drawing on her knowledge of cognitive development, which instructional adjustment is MOST likely to address the underlying developmental need?
options: Increasing the volume of independent silent reading time so students encounter more vocabulary
Replacing comprehension tasks with additional decoding drills until fluency rates increase
Assigning weekly spelling lists that emphasize the multisyllabic patterns students already know
Providing explicit modeling and guided practice of strategies that connect new text to prior knowledge
questions.rationale: At this developmental stage, comprehension breakdowns often reflect a gap in metacognitive and schema-building strategies rather than decoding. Explicit modeling that links text to prior knowledge scaffolds the cognitive processes needed to construct meaning.

questions.stem: A ninth-grade teacher notices that several students can solve algebra problems mechanically but cannot explain why a procedure works or apply it to an unfamiliar context. Considering principles of cognitive and intellectual development, which interpretation BEST explains this pattern?
options: The students are developmentally incapable of abstract reasoning until late adolescence
The students lack the prerequisite arithmetic skills required for algebraic computation
The students have not yet been exposed to enough varied problem types to memorize them all
The students are operating at a procedural level and need tasks that promote abstract, conceptual reasoning
questions.rationale: Successful mechanical computation paired with an inability to explain or transfer signals reliance on procedural knowledge without conceptual understanding. Adolescents are capable of abstract reasoning, so the appropriate response is tasks that bridge procedure to concept.

questions.stem: Mr. Tran observes that his kindergarten students learn new concepts most durably when they manipulate objects before discussing abstract ideas. Which understanding of young children's development BEST justifies designing lessons this way?
options: Young children retain information only when it is presented through technology
Concrete, hands-on experiences support cognitive development before children reason about abstractions
Kindergartners cannot benefit from any verbal explanation of new ideas
Repetition of worksheets is the most reliable path to conceptual understanding
questions.rationale: Young children typically build understanding through concrete, manipulative experiences that precede and ground abstract reasoning, consistent with developmental theory about how early learners construct knowledge.

questions.stem: In a seventh-grade science class, Ms. Becker wants to design a unit that respects students' developing capacity for social comparison and peer evaluation while protecting their self-esteem. Which design choice BEST aligns instruction with adolescents' social-emotional development?
options: Assigning the same fixed ability groups all year so students know their standing
Posting a ranked leaderboard of test scores to motivate competition among students
Calling on students randomly and correcting their errors publicly to build resilience
Using flexible, skill-based collaborative groups in which each member contributes a distinct role
questions.rationale: Early adolescents are highly sensitive to peer perception. Flexible, role-based collaborative groups let students contribute and be valued while minimizing the threat to self-esteem that public ranking creates.

questions.stem: A high school teacher finds that a unit on persuasive writing engages students far more when topics connect to issues in their own community. Which principle of adolescent development BEST explains the increased engagement?
options: Adolescents learn best only when grades are attached to every assignment
Adolescents are unable to engage with content outside their immediate experience
Adolescents prefer abstract content disconnected from real-world application
Adolescents' developing sense of identity and social awareness increases motivation for personally relevant tasks
questions.rationale: Adolescence is marked by identity formation and growing social consciousness, so tasks tied to personally and socially relevant issues tend to boost intrinsic motivation and engagement.

questions.stem: Ms. Ortega plans physical activities for her first-grade students and wants the tasks to match their developmental level. Which consideration is MOST important when accounting for these young learners' physical development?
options: Gross motor skills are still developing, so frequent movement and large-muscle activities are appropriate
Physical development is unrelated to how lessons should be structured
Fine motor skills are fully developed, so detailed handwriting tasks should dominate the day
Children this age require no movement breaks because they sit still easily
questions.rationale: First graders are still refining gross motor skills and benefit from frequent movement and large-muscle activity. Recognizing this developmental reality leads to appropriately structured, active lessons.

questions.stem: Mr. Diallo teaches eleventh grade and notices a student who reasons logically about science problems but makes impulsive decisions in peer conflicts. Understanding adolescent brain development, which interpretation is MOST accurate?
options: The student is intellectually gifted but socially defiant by choice
The student needs to be removed from challenging academic content until behavior improves
The student's logical reasoning proves emotional impulsivity cannot be developmental
The student's cognitive ability and emotional self-regulation are developing at different rates
questions.rationale: Adolescent cognitive capacities often advance ahead of the brain systems governing impulse control and emotional regulation, so strong reasoning can coexist with impulsive social decisions.

questions.stem: A fourth-grade teacher wants to use her knowledge of the zone of proximal development to plan reading instruction. Which approach BEST reflects this concept?
options: Selecting tasks slightly beyond what students can do alone and providing temporary support
Withholding any teacher assistance so students develop independence quickly
Assigning every student texts they can already read independently with no errors
Giving all students identical grade-level texts regardless of their current reading level
questions.rationale: The zone of proximal development describes the range between what a learner can do independently and what they can do with support. Effective instruction targets tasks just beyond independent ability and scaffolds them.

questions.stem: Ms. Park notices that a second-grade student understands a concept perfectly when working with a partner but struggles when working alone. Which instructional response BEST supports the student's progress toward independence?
options: Concluding that the student cannot learn the concept without help
Gradually reducing support through fading scaffolds as the student demonstrates competence
Removing all peer support immediately to force independent work
Permanently pairing the student with a partner for all future tasks
questions.rationale: Gradually fading scaffolds as competence grows moves the learner from supported performance toward independent mastery, which is the goal of working within the zone of proximal development.

questions.stem: Mr. Reyes teaches a fifth-grade class with wide variation in readiness, interest, and learning profile. He wants to differentiate a unit on ecosystems without lowering expectations for any student. Which approach BEST reflects responsible differentiation?
options: Varying the process and product students use to reach the same essential understandings
Grouping students permanently by ability and assigning each group different standards
Giving struggling students fewer learning objectives and advanced students extra worksheets
Allowing students to opt out of the most challenging concepts if they prefer
questions.rationale: Effective differentiation holds the essential understandings constant for all students while varying the process, content access, or product. This maintains high expectations while honoring diverse readiness and profiles.

questions.stem: A new teacher in a linguistically diverse middle school wants to support emergent bilingual students in a content-area class without isolating them. Which strategy is MOST appropriate as a first instructional step?
options: Translating all lessons into students' home languages and stopping English instruction
Postponing content instruction until students are fully proficient in English
Seating emergent bilingual students together in a separate area for simplified work
Providing comprehensible input with visuals, sentence frames, and structured peer interaction
questions.rationale: Emergent bilingual students learn content and language simultaneously when teachers provide comprehensible input supported by visuals, sentence frames, and structured interaction. This keeps them engaged with grade-level content while developing English.

questions.stem: Ms. Chen reviews assessment data showing that three students with identified learning disabilities consistently understand math concepts orally but score poorly on written tests. Which adjustment BEST addresses their needs while preserving the assessed standard?
options: Lowering the difficulty of the math standard being assessed for these students
Excusing the students from the assessment entirely
Providing an accommodation such as allowing oral responses or extended time
Grading the students only on participation rather than mastery
questions.rationale: An accommodation changes how a student accesses or demonstrates learning without altering the standard. Allowing oral responses or extended time lets these students show what they know on the same content.

questions.stem: Mr. Okafor has a gifted student who finishes assignments quickly and shows signs of boredom and disengagement. Which response BEST meets the student's needs without simply assigning more work?
options: Giving the student additional problems identical to those already mastered
Allowing the student to tutor classmates whenever finished, in place of new learning
Providing tiered, open-ended tasks that increase depth and complexity of thinking
Reducing the student's workload so there is less to feel bored about
questions.rationale: Gifted learners need depth and complexity, not more of the same. Tiered, open-ended tasks extend their thinking and sustain engagement while keeping them challenged at an appropriate level.

questions.stem: A teacher receives an Individualized Education Program (IEP) for a new student that specifies a quiet testing environment and frequent breaks. Which statement BEST describes the teacher's responsibility regarding these provisions?
options: The provisions are legally required and must be implemented consistently
The provisions can be disregarded if the teacher believes the student does not need them
The provisions are optional suggestions the teacher may use at her discretion
The provisions apply only on standardized tests, not in daily classroom work
questions.rationale: An IEP is a legally binding document. Accommodations such as a quiet testing environment and frequent breaks must be implemented consistently across applicable settings.

questions.stem: Ms. Lund wants to ensure that her instructional materials represent diverse perspectives and avoid stereotypes. Which is the MOST appropriate first step when selecting texts for her class?
options: Choosing only texts that reflect the majority culture to keep content familiar
Reviewing materials for varied perspectives and inclusive, non-stereotypical representation
Avoiding any text that mentions cultural differences to prevent controversy
Selecting texts solely based on reading level without regard to representation
questions.rationale: Reviewing materials for diverse perspectives and inclusive representation ensures all students see themselves reflected and encounter varied viewpoints, supporting equity in the curriculum.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that a student who recently experienced housing instability is frequently tired and unprepared. Which response BEST reflects sensitivity to the student's circumstances while maintaining learning expectations?
options: Ignoring the situation since home circumstances are outside the teacher's role
Publicly reminding the student to come prepared like everyone else
Lowering academic standards permanently because of the student's situation
Privately connecting the student with support resources and adjusting non-essential requirements
questions.rationale: A responsive teacher privately addresses the student's needs, connects them with appropriate support, and adjusts non-essential demands while keeping learning expectations intact and protecting the student's dignity.

questions.stem: Mr. Salazar plans a project that allows students to demonstrate their understanding of a historical event through writing, art, a podcast, or a model. Which principle of meeting diverse learning needs does this BEST illustrate?
options: Eliminating standards so every student can succeed easily
Offering multiple means of expression so students can show learning in varied ways
Reducing rigor for students who choose non-writing options
Assigning the same product to all students for fair comparison
questions.rationale: Providing multiple means of expression lets students demonstrate the same understanding through different modalities, addressing diverse strengths while holding the learning goal constant.

questions.stem: A teacher has a student with attention difficulties who becomes overwhelmed by multi-step directions. Which instructional adjustment is the BEST first step to support the student's access to learning?
options: Removing the student from group activities to work alone on simplified content
Breaking tasks into smaller steps and checking for understanding after each
Waiting until the student fails the task to provide any support
Giving the student the same lengthy directions but speaking them more loudly
questions.rationale: Chunking complex directions into smaller, sequenced steps with comprehension checks reduces cognitive overload and gives the student manageable entry points to the same learning.

questions.stem: Mr. Adeyemi plans to teach a complex skill: writing a research-based argument. He wants his lesson sequence to follow sound instructional design. Which ordering of activities BEST reflects the gradual release of responsibility?
options: Group practice, then independent essay, then teacher modeling
Teacher modeling, then guided collaborative practice, then independent writing
Independent writing, then guided practice, then teacher feedback only
Independent essay, then teacher modeling, then guided group practice
questions.rationale: Gradual release moves from teacher modeling ('I do'), to guided collaborative practice ('we do'), to independent application ('you do'), progressively transferring responsibility to students.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to increase higher-order thinking during a class discussion about a novel. Which question is MOST likely to elicit analysis rather than recall?
options: In what year was the novel published?
What is the title of the first chapter?
Who is the main character in the novel?
How does the author use the setting to reflect the protagonist's internal conflict?
questions.rationale: Analysis questions require students to examine relationships among parts of a text. Asking how setting reflects internal conflict prompts students to interpret and connect elements rather than recall facts.

questions.stem: Ms. Donovan notices that during a lecture-heavy lesson, student attention fades after about fifteen minutes. Drawing on principles of effective instructional design, which adjustment is the BEST first step?
options: Lengthening the lecture so students hear the content more times
Interspersing brief active-engagement tasks to break up direct instruction
Assigning the same content as homework instead of teaching it
Removing all direct instruction in favor of unstructured discovery
questions.rationale: Breaking direct instruction into shorter segments interspersed with active-engagement tasks maintains attention and processing, improving learning compared with extended passive lecture.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to transfer a problem-solving strategy from math class to real-world situations. Which instructional design choice MOST effectively promotes transfer of learning?
options: Limiting practice to a single worked example demonstrated by the teacher
Telling students the strategy will be useful someday without further connection
Providing varied contexts and prompting students to articulate when and why to apply the strategy
Having students practice the strategy only with identical textbook problems
questions.rationale: Transfer is promoted when students practice a strategy across varied contexts and reflect on the conditions for its use. This builds the flexible, conditional knowledge needed to apply learning in new situations.

questions.stem: Mr. Liang wants to activate prior knowledge before introducing a unit on weather systems. Which opening activity BEST serves this purpose?
options: Administering a graded multiple-choice test on weather terminology
Leading a brief brainstorm in which students share what they already notice about local weather
Lecturing on the definitions students will need for the unit
Assigning a chapter to read silently before any discussion
questions.rationale: Activating prior knowledge connects new content to what students already know. A brief brainstorm surfaces existing ideas and primes students to integrate new learning meaningfully.

questions.stem: A teacher designing a lesson realizes her planned activities are engaging but only loosely connected to the stated learning objective. Which principle of effective planning should guide her revision?
options: Assessment should be designed after teaching, independent of the objective
The objective should be changed to match whichever activities are most fun
Activities, assessment, and objectives should be aligned so each supports the intended learning
Activities should be chosen for novelty regardless of the objective
questions.rationale: Effective planning requires alignment among objectives, instructional activities, and assessment so that what is taught and measured supports the intended learning. Engaging but misaligned activities should be revised to fit the objective.

questions.stem: Ms. Faber wants to end each lesson in a way that helps students consolidate what they learned. Which closing activity BEST achieves this purpose?
options: Having students write a brief summary of the lesson's key idea and one remaining question
Dismissing students early once the main activity is finished
Collecting materials silently with no review of the day's learning
Starting the next lesson's content to save time
questions.rationale: A reflective closure that asks students to summarize the key idea and pose a question consolidates learning and gives the teacher formative insight into understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher is integrating technology into a research unit. Which use of technology MOST meaningfully enhances learning rather than simply digitizing a task?
options: Having students type notes that they would otherwise handwrite
Using a collaborative platform for students to co-construct, cite, and revise a shared analysis
Showing a video in place of reading without any follow-up task
Replacing a printed worksheet with an identical on-screen worksheet
questions.rationale: Technology meaningfully enhances learning when it enables tasks not easily done otherwise, such as real-time collaborative construction, citation, and revision of a shared analysis, deepening engagement and skills.

questions.stem: Mr. Petrov gives a quick exit ticket midway through a unit and finds that most students hold a common misconception about fractions. Which use of this assessment information is MOST appropriate?
options: Recording the scores in the gradebook and moving on to the next topic
Reteaching the entire unit from the beginning for all students
Assuming the misconception will resolve itself with more practice problems
Adjusting upcoming instruction to directly address the identified misconception
questions.rationale: Formative assessment exists to inform instruction. Using exit-ticket data to target the specific misconception before moving on is the purpose of the assessment and supports learning responsively.

questions.stem: Mr. Castillo notices that one of his unit-test items was answered incorrectly by nearly every student, including his strongest performers. What is the MOST appropriate professional response?
options: Remove the topic from future instruction since students cannot learn it
Keep the item unchanged because tests should never be revised
Assume the whole class failed to study that topic and lower their grades accordingly
Examine the item for ambiguity or misalignment and consider whether it validly measured the objective
questions.rationale: When even strong students miss an item, the teacher should examine the item's validity, checking for ambiguous wording or misalignment with what was taught, before drawing conclusions about student learning.

questions.stem: Ms. Greer wants to use ongoing checks during a lesson to monitor understanding and adjust her teaching in real time. Which assessment approach BEST fits this purpose?
options: A cumulative final exam given at the end of the semester
Frequent formative checks such as quick polls and brief written responses during the lesson
A standardized test administered once in the spring
A single graded project submitted at the unit's conclusion
questions.rationale: Formative checks embedded throughout a lesson, such as quick polls and short written responses, give the teacher real-time evidence to adjust instruction immediately, matching the stated purpose.

questions.stem: Ms. Alvarado teaches fourth grade and notices that Diego, a typically engaged student, has stopped participating in group work over the past two weeks and now puts his head down during transitions. Knowing that this age group is forming a sense of competence and peer belonging, what is the most developmentally appropriate FIRST step for Ms. Alvarado?
options: Announce to the class that everyone must participate fully or lose recess privileges for the week
Speak privately with Diego in a low-pressure setting to understand possible changes in his social or emotional experience
Refer Diego directly to special education evaluation because of the sudden change in engagement
Move Diego's seat away from his group and require him to complete all tasks independently until his behavior improves
questions.rationale: A sudden behavioral and engagement change in a child at this developmental stage often signals a social or emotional concern. The teacher should first gather information through a supportive, private conversation before drawing conclusions or taking punitive or referral action.
