questions.rationale: Effectiveness and alignment matter most.

questions.stem: A teacher helps students understand that comments they post online can be permanent and public. This lesson is part of
options: Digital citizenship and digital footprint awareness
Keyboarding instruction
Coding
Computer repair
questions.rationale: Digital citizenship includes understanding online permanence.

questions.stem: A teacher uses video conferencing so that a student who is homebound can participate in class. Which principle does this support?
options: Replacing the need for instruction
Reducing the student's workload
Removing the student's responsibilities
Access and inclusion through technology
questions.rationale: Technology can extend access.

questions.stem: A teacher uses an online discussion board where students respond to each other's posts. What is a benefit compared with a whole-class spoken discussion?
options: All students must respond immediately
The teacher cannot monitor participation
Students who need more time to think or are less comfortable speaking can contribute thoughtfully
The discussion cannot be saved
questions.rationale: Asynchronous tools provide processing time.

questions.stem: A teacher tracks students' digital reading data in an app. Which practice best protects student privacy?
options: Post class data publicly on social media
Share logins with friends
Store data on a personal device without protection
Use only approved platforms, share data only with authorized personnel, and avoid posting identifiable data publicly
questions.rationale: Student data must be protected under FERPA and district policy.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a five-question exit ticket on solving two-step equations and sorts the responses into three piles: correct, partially correct, and off-track. What is the best use of the sorted piles?
options: Discard the tickets because they are only practice
Hand the papers back without comment and continue the pacing guide
Record each pile's count as a grade for the unit
Plan the next day's small groups and a short reteach for the off-track pile
questions.rationale: Sorting responses turns evidence into instructional grouping decisions.

questions.stem: After a quiz, a teacher returns papers with comments only, no scores, and asks students to revise one answer. A colleague worries students will not care. What research-based point supports the teacher's choice?
options: Comments alone tend to produce more attention to the feedback than grades paired with comments
Grades always motivate students more than any written comments
Comments are less accurate than numerical scores
Students learn best when they receive no information about their errors
questions.rationale: Research shows that grades can draw attention away from the feedback content.

questions.stem: Which feedback statement is most descriptive rather than evaluative?
options: "This is better than most."
"You are bad at graphs."
"Nice work."
"Your graph includes a title and labeled axes, but the scale on the y-axis skips values."
questions.rationale: Descriptive feedback states what is present and what is missing relative to criteria.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that after a low unit test most students did not read her comments. Which routine best increases use of feedback?
options: Collect the tests again immediately
Return tests on the last day of the week without discussion
Tell students to read the comments at home
Give class time to read comments, set one goal, and plan how to apply it on the next task
questions.rationale: Feedback needs structured time to be used.

questions.stem: A teacher regularly uses the phrase "Where am I going? Where am I now? How do I close the gap?" with students. Which feedback framework does this reflect?
options: Hattie and Timperley's three feedback questions: feed up, feed back, and feed forward
Bloom's taxonomy of cognitive levels
Kounin's model of lesson momentum
Piaget's stages of cognitive development
questions.rationale: Effective feedback addresses goals, current status, and next steps.

questions.stem: A student asks, "Is this good?" about a rough draft. Which teacher response best moves the student forward?
options: "What part are you most proud of, and which part do you want help with?"
"It's fine."
"I'll grade it later."
"Don't worry about it."
questions.rationale: Questions engage the student in self-assessment and shape feedback.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a rubric with four levels, and a student asks why her work is a 3 instead of a 4. What is the best response?
options: Say that the teacher decides by feel
Say that only a few students ever earn a 4
Point to the specific criterion language that differs and show an example of work at level 4
Give the student a 4 to avoid conflict
questions.rationale: Rubric language and exemplars clarify expectations.

questions.stem: Students in a class consistently score well on tests but cannot explain their reasoning when asked. Which change to assessment would most effectively reveal this gap?
options: Add items that require students to justify answers or explain a solution path
Increase the number of true-false items
Shorten the time limit for tests
Replace all tests with matching
questions.rationale: Constructed-response tasks reveal depth of understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher keeps a spreadsheet with each student's results by standard rather than just an overall percentage. What is the main benefit?
options: She can avoid giving feedback
She can reduce the number of assessments
She can see which specific standards each student has or has not mastered
She can rank students from best to worst
questions.rationale: Standards-level data supports targeted instruction.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a four-corners activity where students move to the corner that matches their answer, then discuss why. Which purpose does this primarily serve?
options: Making student thinking visible and prompting discussion about reasoning
Assigning final grades
Replacing all other assessments
Ranking students by speed
questions.rationale: Physical response strategies reveal thinking and engage students.

questions.stem: A teacher asks students to explain, in writing, why a particular wrong answer is wrong. Which learning benefit is most likely?
options: Students clarify misconceptions and strengthen understanding of the correct idea
Students memorize the wrong answer
Students avoid future errors without further instruction
Students lose confidence in all answers
questions.rationale: Error explanation deepens understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that one student's performance on tests is consistently lower than on classroom tasks. Which step best helps determine the cause?
options: Lower all of the student's grades
Observe the student during tests, review accommodations, and gather additional evidence of learning
Assume the student is cheating on classroom tasks
Stop giving tests to the student
questions.rationale: Understanding causes requires more data.

questions.stem: A teacher uses an item analysis report and finds that an item on theme in literature has a p-value of 0.30 and a negative discrimination index. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Keep the item because difficult items are always good
Review the item for flaws such as a miskeyed answer or confusing wording before using the results
Reveal the answer to the class and keep the scores
Add more items just like it
questions.rationale: A negative discrimination index suggests a problem with the item.

questions.stem: A teacher uses self-assessment and peer assessment before submitting a lab report. What is the main benefit?
options: The teacher no longer needs to evaluate the report
Students stop caring about quality
Students learn to apply criteria and revise before the teacher's final evaluation
Peers assign the final grade
questions.rationale: Using criteria builds assessment literacy.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to know exactly where they stand toward a standard. Which tool is best?
options: A learning progression or proficiency scale with clear descriptors for each level
A list of the teacher's favorite students
A single letter grade with no explanation
A class ranking posted on the wall
questions.rationale: Learning progressions show levels toward a goal.

questions.stem: A teacher offers students a choice of redoing a project for a higher grade after completing a reflection that identifies what they will change. Which principle does this reflect?
options: Grades as a reflection of learning, supported by opportunities to improve
Grades as a punishment for early mistakes
Grades as a reward for compliance
Grades as a ranking tool only
questions.rationale: Redoing work after reflection emphasizes growth.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a pre-assessment and discovers that 80 percent of students already know the content. What should she do?
options: Give a grade for the pre-assessment
Teach the entire unit as planned
Compact the unit and move to more complex content
Repeat the pre-assessment
questions.rationale: Using data to adjust pacing avoids repetition.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to record observations during small-group instruction quickly. Which tool is most efficient?
options: A standardized test for each group
A long essay written after each group
A memory of all students without notes
A clipboard with a class roster and space for brief notes on each student's performance
questions.rationale: Quick notes capture evidence for later use.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to share a student's progress with the family at the start of a parent-teacher conference. Which opening is most effective?
options: Start by asking the parent to explain the student's behavior
Start with specific strengths and examples of work, then discuss goals and next steps
Start with a list of the student's problems
Start by comparing the student to siblings
questions.rationale: Strength-based openings build trust.

questions.stem: A teacher sends a weekly email to families that includes upcoming topics, ways to support learning at home, and a celebration of class successes. What is the primary purpose?
options: To report grades for every student
To replace all conferences
To keep families informed and engaged as partners in learning
To avoid contact with families
questions.rationale: Regular communication builds partnership.

questions.stem: A family tells a teacher they distrust the school because of past negative experiences. Which response best builds a relationship?
options: Suggest that they should be more cooperative
Listen without defensiveness, acknowledge their experiences, and communicate consistently with respect
Stop communicating with the family
Tell them the past is irrelevant
questions.rationale: Trust develops through respect and consistency.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to involve families in a unit about local history. Which activity is most inclusive?
options: Require parents to attend a daytime event
Invite families to share stories, photos, or interviews in ways that fit their schedules and languages
Ask only parents who speak English to share
Assign students to complete the project alone
questions.rationale: Flexible participation invites all families.

questions.stem: A teacher must communicate a student's serious behavior concern to parents. Which approach is best?
options: Describe the student as a bad kid
Wait until the end of the semester to mention it
Send an email with only a punishment announcement
Contact the family promptly, describe observed behavior factually, and invite collaboration on a plan
questions.rationale: Factual and collaborative communication is respectful and effective.

questions.stem: A family says they want to help with reading but do not know how. Which suggestion is most helpful?
options: Tell them to stay out of it
Suggest they hire a tutor immediately
Offer a few simple strategies, such as reading together for ten minutes and asking questions, and provide materials
Give them a long list of academic terms
questions.rationale: Practical, simple strategies empower families.

questions.stem: A teacher uses interpreters and translated materials for families who speak languages other than English. Which principle does this practice reflect?
options: Eliminating parent conferences
Meaningful access to information and participation for all families
Avoiding two-way conversation
Reducing the amount of communication
questions.rationale: Language access is a key part of family partnership.

questions.stem: A teacher organizes student-led conferences. What is a key benefit?
options: Parents are excluded from the conversation
Students take responsibility for explaining their learning and setting goals with their families
Teachers no longer need to prepare
Only high-achieving students participate
questions.rationale: Student-led conferences build ownership.

questions.stem: A parent asks how to help her child with a math assignment but says she was never good at math. What is the best teacher response?
options: Tell her to do the homework for the child
Suggest that math is not for everyone
Tell her not to help
Encourage her to ask her child to explain the work and share a few hints or resources
questions.rationale: Supporting thinking and offering resources helps.

questions.stem: A teacher is concerned that a student may be experiencing difficulties at home, but there is no evidence of abuse. What is the most appropriate way to communicate with the family?
options: Express care, share observations about school behavior, and offer to connect the family with campus resources
Accuse the family of neglect
Share the concerns with other students
Avoid contacting the family
questions.rationale: Supportive outreach respects families and helps students.

questions.stem: A teacher keeps a communication log that records dates and summaries of contacts with families. What is the main purpose?
options: To document communication and track follow-up
To limit the number of contacts
To replace report cards
To share with other families
questions.rationale: Logs help maintain consistent communication.

questions.stem: A school hosts a family literacy night. Which feature makes the event more accessible?
options: Offering materials only in English
Providing childcare, translation, and refreshments at a time that suits working families
Scheduling the event during the workday
Requiring RSVPs weeks ahead
questions.rationale: Removing barriers increases attendance.

questions.stem: A teacher observes a colleague's lesson using a protocol that focuses on student engagement and then meets to discuss it. What is the primary purpose of peer observation?
options: To learn from one another's practice and reflect on instruction
To evaluate the colleague for employment decisions
To criticize the colleague publicly
To replace formal appraisals
questions.rationale: Peer observation supports shared growth.

questions.stem: A new teacher asks a veteran for advice about managing transitions. Which behavior by the veteran best supports professional growth?
options: Share specific strategies, invite the new teacher to observe, and offer to observe in return
Judge the new teacher harshly
Take over the new teacher's class
Tell the new teacher to figure it out alone
questions.rationale: Collegial support builds practice.

questions.stem: A grade-level team reviews common assessment data and finds that one teacher's students outperformed others on a standard. What is the most professional way to use this finding?
options: Invite the teacher to share instructional strategies and plan to try them across classrooms
Ask the teacher to stop sharing materials
Hide the data to avoid conflict
Blame the other teachers for poor results
questions.rationale: Teams learn from effective practices.

questions.stem: A teacher sets a professional goal to increase the use of higher-order questions and tracks progress by recording the questions she asks in three lessons. This reflects
options: Compliance only
Avoiding feedback
Reflective practice using evidence to improve instruction
A random change in behavior
questions.rationale: Goal setting and data collection support growth.

questions.stem: A teacher disagrees with a colleague about grading practices. Which action is most professional?
options: Ignore the colleague forever
Complain to students
Post a complaint on social media
Discuss concerns privately and focus on shared goals, using data when possible
questions.rationale: Professional disagreement is handled respectfully.

questions.stem: In a school with a campus improvement plan, teachers are asked to contribute to goals for reading growth. Which action reflects professional responsibility?
options: Work only on individual goals unrelated to the plan
Align classroom practices with the plan and share evidence of progress with the team
Resist all changes
Ignore the plan because it is administrative
questions.rationale: Teachers support shared goals.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to mentor a student teacher. Which practice best supports the student teacher's development?
options: Critique every minor detail without suggestions
Give the student teacher full responsibility on the first day
Model effective practice, provide regular feedback, and gradually increase responsibility
Leave the student teacher alone for the entire semester
questions.rationale: Effective mentoring involves modeling and gradual release.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to improve her use of data and chooses a professional learning activity. Which option is most likely to change her practice?
options: A one-hour lecture with no practice
A series of workshops with coaching in her classroom and time to analyze her own students' data
A reading list she never discusses
An online video with no follow-up
questions.rationale: Practice, coaching, and application change behavior.

questions.stem: A teacher records a lesson to watch and reflect on her questioning. Which professional practice is she using?
options: Peer evaluation
Test security
Self-observation as a tool for reflection
Summative assessment
questions.rationale: Video review supports self-reflection.

questions.stem: A teacher works with the school counselor, special education teacher, and family to plan supports for a student. This is an example of
options: A disciplinary hearing
A grade appeal
Collaborative teaming to meet a student's needs
An unnecessary meeting
questions.rationale: Collaboration across roles supports students.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to share a lesson with a team and receive feedback. She feels nervous. Which mindset best supports growth?
options: Defend every choice regardless of evidence
View feedback as information to improve instruction rather than a judgment of worth
Dismiss colleagues' opinions
Avoid all feedback to protect pride
questions.rationale: A growth mindset welcomes feedback.

questions.stem: A teacher joins a book study with colleagues to read about formative assessment and try one strategy each month. What is the main benefit?
options: Replacing formal training
Collective learning and shared accountability for applying new ideas
Reducing collaboration
Avoiding any change in practice
questions.rationale: Learning communities support implementation.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to supervise a paraprofessional who works with students needing support. Which practice is most appropriate?
options: Provide clear directions, plan together, and give regular feedback
Criticize the paraprofessional in front of students
Avoid discussing student needs
Leave the paraprofessional to decide all instruction
questions.rationale: Supervision involves direction and communication.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that her instruction is not meeting the needs of English learners and asks a campus specialist for help. This is an example of
options: Using professional resources and collaboration to improve instruction
Delegating all teaching to the specialist
Avoiding responsibility
Showing a lack of competence that should be hidden
questions.rationale: Seeking help is a sign of professionalism.

questions.stem: A Texas teacher learns that a colleague has been sending private messages to a student that include flattery and requests to keep the conversations secret. What should the teacher do?
options: Ask the student to stop responding and take no further action
Report the concern to the campus administrator or district official promptly, following district procedures
Confront the colleague privately and wait to see whether the messages stop
Wait until there is proof of physical contact before reporting
questions.rationale: Educators have an obligation to report suspected inappropriate educator-student communication, and delay can put students at risk.

questions.stem: Under the Texas Educators' Code of Ethics, which action by a teacher is most clearly prohibited?
options: Revealing confidential student information that is not necessary for a lawful professional purpose
Participating in a professional association
Sharing instructional strategies with colleagues
Communicating with parents about student progress
questions.rationale: The Code prohibits disclosure of confidential student information unless required by law or serving a lawful professional purpose.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked by a parent to change a grade because the parent is a school board member. Which response aligns with ethical standards?
options: Change the grade only if the parent offers to volunteer
Decline to change the grade without evidence of learning and explain the grading criteria
Give extra credit to all students
Change the grade to avoid conflict with the board member
questions.rationale: Educators must not use their position or yield to influence to falsify records.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a student as a babysitter and pays the student cash for childcare at the teacher's home. Which concern is most relevant?
options: The arrangement is permitted because it is off campus
The arrangement may blur professional boundaries and create a conflict of interest
The arrangement is required by district policy
The arrangement violates copyright law
questions.rationale: Dual relationships with students risk boundary violations.

questions.stem: Which person is a mandated reporter of suspected child abuse in Texas?
options: Any professional who has regular contact with children, including teachers
Only licensed social workers
Only school nurses
Only school police officers
questions.rationale: Texas law requires professionals, including teachers, to report suspected abuse or neglect.

questions.stem: A student discloses abuse and asks the teacher to promise not to tell anyone. What should the teacher say?
options: "I'll wait to see if it happens again before I do anything."
"I care about you and I have to tell people who can help keep you safe."
"I promise I won't tell anyone."
"Let's keep it our secret until you're ready."
questions.rationale: Teachers cannot promise confidentiality when abuse is disclosed.

questions.stem: A teacher learns that a student is being cyberbullied by classmates on social media after school. What should the teacher do?
options: Tell the student to delete the account
Ignore it because it happened off campus
Report the situation according to district policy so administrators can investigate and support the student
Post the bullies' names on the class website
questions.rationale: Texas law requires reporting and response procedures for bullying, including cyberbullying.

questions.stem: Which statement about copyright is accurate for teachers?
options: Educational use does not automatically make copying legal, and each use must be evaluated under fair use or another exception
Teachers may copy entire books if they credit the author
Teachers may copy any material for classroom use
Copyright does not apply to materials found online
questions.rationale: Fair use is a case-by-case analysis.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to play a song from a streaming service for a school-wide assembly open to the public. What is the best step?
options: Play the song because it is educational
Play the song because students are present
Play the song because it is short
Check whether the district holds a public performance license or obtain permission
questions.rationale: Public performance may require licensing.

questions.stem: A teacher is writing an IEP goal for a student and a parent asks for the goal to be changed. What does IDEA require?
options: Parents may be excluded from meetings
Teachers make all decisions without parent input
Parents may attend only if invited by the principal
Parents are equal members of the team, and their input must be considered in decisions
questions.rationale: IDEA ensures meaningful parent participation.

questions.stem: A district proposes to change a student's placement to a more restrictive setting. What must the district provide to the parents?
options: An oral notice only
Prior written notice describing the proposed change and the reasons for it
No notice if the change is temporary
A notice sent after the change takes effect
questions.rationale: IDEA requires prior written notice before changes in identification, evaluation, or placement.

questions.stem: A teacher is unsure whether a student's behavior is a manifestation of the student's disability. Who determines this?
options: A group that includes the parent and relevant members of the ARD committee in a manifestation determination review
The student's classmates
The principal alone
The teacher alone
questions.rationale: The MDR is conducted by the school, parent, and relevant ARD members.

questions.stem: A student with a 504 plan is being considered for discipline. Which statement is accurate?
options: A review should determine whether the behavior is related to the disability before certain disciplinary actions are taken
Discipline decisions are made by the student
504 students cannot be disciplined at all
504 students have no disciplinary protections
questions.rationale: Section 504 requires consideration of the disability in disciplinary changes of placement.

questions.stem: A parent requests an evaluation for special education in writing. What is the district's obligation in Texas?
options: To evaluate without any parent consent
To ignore the request until the end of the year
To require the parent to pay for the evaluation
To respond within a specified timeline, either by seeking consent for evaluation or providing prior written notice of refusal
questions.rationale: Districts must respond to written requests within required timelines.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to take students on a field trip involving a bus. Which action best protects student safety and addresses legal responsibility?
options: Allow students to travel independently to the site
Follow district procedures for approvals, permission slips, supervision ratios, and emergency plans
Rely on verbal permission from students
Skip the permission slip for short trips
questions.rationale: Following procedures meets duty of care.

questions.stem: A student is injured when a teacher is out of the room. Which legal concept is most relevant to determining the teacher's liability?
options: Whether the teacher breached the duty to provide reasonable supervision and whether the injury was foreseeable
Whether the student wore the correct uniform
Whether the teacher has tenure
Whether the school has a mascot
questions.rationale: Negligence requires duty, breach, causation, and damages.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to give medication to a student. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Give the medication because the parent asked
Follow district policy, which typically limits administration to authorized personnel with proper documentation
Give a different medication if it seems similar
Give the medication if the student asks
questions.rationale: Medication administration is regulated.

questions.stem: A teacher sees a student with a possible seizure. What should the teacher do?
options: Restrain the student's movements
Place an object in the student's mouth
Continue the lesson and ignore it
Follow the emergency plan, keep the student safe, and call for medical help according to procedure
questions.rationale: Emergency procedures prioritize safety.

questions.stem: Which behavior is consistent with professional ethics when communicating with students electronically?
options: Using private social media accounts to message students
Using district-approved platforms and keeping communication focused on school matters
Asking students to keep messages secret
Texting students late at night about personal matters
questions.rationale: Professional communication is transparent.

questions.stem: A teacher discovers that a student has posted threatening statements about harming classmates. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Delete the post and say nothing
Wait to see whether the student follows through
Notify administrators immediately and follow the district's threat assessment and safety procedures
Discuss the post with other students
questions.rationale: Threats require immediate reporting.

questions.stem: A teacher is aware that a student is carrying a weapon. What is the correct action?
options: Notify administrators immediately and follow emergency protocols without confronting the student alone
Search the student's bag alone
Ask the student to hand over the weapon in front of the class
Wait until after class to talk privately
questions.rationale: Safety protocols protect everyone.

questions.stem: A teacher uses physical restraint on a student who is not an immediate danger but is refusing to leave the room. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Restraint is allowed to enforce classroom rules
Restraint is permitted only in emergencies when behavior poses a threat of imminent harm, so this use is inappropriate
Restraint is allowed if the teacher is angry
Restraint is always allowed to enforce compliance
questions.rationale: Texas law limits restraint to emergencies.

questions.stem: A teacher is aware that corporal punishment is allowed only if district policy permits it and parents have not opted out. A parent has provided a written statement opting out. What should the teacher do?
options: Use corporal punishment if the behavior is severe
Ask the student to decide
Ignore the statement
Follow the parent's opt-out and use other approved behavior supports
questions.rationale: Opt-out decisions must be honored.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to share a student's disciplinary record with a prospective employer of the student. What is the correct response?
options: Share a summary orally
Post the record on the school website
Decline and direct the request to administration, since disclosure requires consent
Share the record because the employer asked
questions.rationale: Education records are confidential.

questions.stem: A student transfers to another school district. What does FERPA permit regarding education records?
options: Records must be destroyed
Records may never be transferred
The sending district may send records to the new school without parent consent if its notice states it will do so
Records may be posted online
questions.rationale: FERPA allows disclosure to schools where a student seeks to enroll.

questions.stem: A teacher is approached by a reporter wanting to interview a student about a school event. What should the teacher do?
options: Refer the reporter to the district communications office and not allow the interview without administrative and parent approval
Provide the student's phone number
Provide the student's grades to give context
Allow the interview in class
questions.rationale: Student privacy and district policy govern media contact.

questions.stem: Which action by an educator is an example of a conflict of interest?
options: Recommending a library book
Assigning a textbook adopted by the district
Requiring students to buy a book written by the educator for a profit without district approval
Using a free online resource
questions.rationale: Using position for personal financial gain is a conflict.

questions.stem: A teacher sells cookies for a personal side business to students during class. Which standard is most likely violated?
options: Copyright law
Students' right to free speech
Use of professional position or school time for personal gain
Mandated reporting requirements
questions.rationale: Educators must not use school time or resources for personal business.

questions.stem: A substitute teacher finds that a student is missing a required accommodation noted in the sub plans. What should the substitute do?
options: Assume it is not needed
Provide the accommodation and note any concerns for the regular teacher
Skip the accommodation for convenience
Provide it only if the student asks
questions.rationale: Accommodations must be implemented consistently.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to display student artwork in a public gallery. Which step best protects student privacy and rights?
options: Display the work without any consent
Obtain parent permission and follow district policy before display with identifying information
Sell the artwork
Display the work with full names and addresses
questions.rationale: Public display with identifying information requires consent.

questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates an educator's responsibility to follow school and district policies?
options: Ignoring policies that seem inconvenient
Following policies only when observed
Creating personal policies
Reading and following the employee handbook and asking for clarification when unsure
questions.rationale: Following policy is a professional responsibility.

questions.stem: A teacher believes that a district policy violates a student's rights. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Post the concern on social media
Raise the concern through the chain of command and seek clarification from administration or legal counsel
Violate the policy secretly
Encourage students to protest
questions.rationale: Professional channels address concerns.

questions.stem: A parent asks a teacher to help the family apply for a government benefit by sharing the teacher's personal information. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Refer the family to the campus social worker or counselor who can assist appropriately
Complete the application with false information
Ignore the request
Share the teacher's Social Security number
questions.rationale: Referral to appropriate staff protects boundaries.

questions.stem: A teacher notices another teacher is frequently late and leaving students unsupervised. What should the teacher do?
options: Report the concern to the administrator since student supervision is a safety issue
Complain on social media
Cover the class without telling anyone
Ignore the problem
questions.rationale: Supervision lapses should be reported.

questions.stem: A student asks to leave class to go to the restroom during a lesson. Which practice best balances student needs with safety?
options: Allow students to leave without any record
Require students to hold it until the bell
Deny all restroom requests
Allow the request following campus procedures such as a sign-out sheet
questions.rationale: Student needs and safety are balanced by procedures.

questions.stem: A teacher is aware that a student's family is facing immigration enforcement fears and the student is anxious. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Ask the student about the family's legal status
Provide a supportive environment, avoid asking about immigration status, and connect the family with school resources
Report the family to authorities
Share the student's situation with the class
questions.rationale: Schools should not inquire about immigration status.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to use a student's essay as an example for future classes. What is the best practice?
options: Obtain the student's permission and remove identifying information
Post the essay with the student's name
Use it without telling the student
Sell the essay to a publisher
questions.rationale: Student work is the student's property and is protected.

questions.stem: A teacher is told by a student that a classmate is planning to run away from home. What is the best response?
options: Tell the whole class
Keep the secret to honor the friend
Tell the student to handle it themselves
Share the information with the counselor or administrator so that they can follow safety procedures
questions.rationale: Safety concerns require adult involvement.

questions.stem: A teacher inadvertently leaves a gradebook open on a classroom computer where students can see it. Which responsibility has been compromised?
options: Providing equal access to technology
Complying with copyright law
Protecting the confidentiality of student education records
Meeting accessibility standards
questions.rationale: Teachers must safeguard records.

questions.stem: A teacher sees a student being treated unfairly by another student because of religion. According to the Code of Ethics, what is the teacher's responsibility?
options: Tell the student to ignore it
Praise the student who is harassing
Protect the student from harassment and follow reporting procedures
Ignore the incident because it is a personal matter
questions.rationale: Teachers must protect students from harassment.

questions.stem: A teacher accepts a handmade card and small token gift from a student at the end of the year. What is the best practice regarding gifts?
options: Refuse all communication from the student
Accept any gift regardless of value
Ask for gifts from students
Follow district policy, which typically allows small tokens of appreciation but discourages costly gifts
questions.rationale: Policies limit gifts to avoid conflicts of interest.

questions.stem: Which situation best illustrates a teacher's duty of confidentiality?
options: A teacher discusses a student in a restaurant
A teacher posts a class roster with grades
A teacher shares a student's test scores publicly
A teacher does not discuss a student's health condition with other parents
questions.rationale: Confidentiality protects student privacy.

questions.stem: A kindergarten teacher notices that children who are read to daily at home recognize more words than peers who are not. Which concept best explains this advantage?
options: Conservation, in which quantity remains constant despite changes in appearance
Operant conditioning, in which reinforcement shapes spoken language
Emergent literacy, in which early exposure to print and talk builds foundations for reading
Egocentrism, in which children cannot view an idea from another perspective
questions.rationale: Emergent literacy views reading development as beginning long before formal instruction.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that fourth graders can classify animals using several attributes but struggle to evaluate a hypothetical situation with no concrete example. Which stage best fits this pattern?
options: Sensorimotor, where learning occurs through reflexes and actions
Concrete operational, where logical thought is tied to tangible examples
Formal operational, where abstract hypotheses are tested systematically
Preoperational, where thinking is dominated by perception and egocentrism
questions.rationale: Concrete operational children reason logically about real objects and events.

questions.stem: A teacher plans a lesson where students watch a more skilled peer solve a problem aloud and then attempt a similar problem with prompts that are gradually removed. Which pair of concepts best frames this plan?
options: Maslow's esteem needs and self-actualization in a hierarchy
Vygotsky's more knowledgeable other and scaffolding within the zone of proximal development
Skinner's continuous reinforcement and extinction of unwanted responses
Piaget's object permanence and animism in the preoperational period
questions.rationale: Guided support that fades as competence increases matches scaffolding in the ZPD.

questions.stem: Which statement about the adolescent brain is most consistent with current research and most useful for a high school teacher?
options: The prefrontal cortex, which supports planning and impulse control, continues to mature into early adulthood
Teens are unable to understand consequences under any circumstances
Brain development is complete by age eight, so older students cannot change how they learn
Brain growth is unaffected by sleep, nutrition, or stress
questions.rationale: Executive function continues to develop, which supports structured routines and explicit instruction in planning.

questions.stem: A teacher asks fifth graders to complete a worksheet about cause and effect using a story the class just read together. This task is appropriate because students at this age
options: Rely entirely on trial-and-error with objects
Can reason logically about concrete content they have experienced directly or through text
Think only in terms of their own perspective
Cannot reason about relationships until adolescence
questions.rationale: Elementary students can use logic with familiar content.

questions.stem: A student who frequently receives praise only for being "smart" avoids challenging tasks to prevent mistakes. Which kind of feedback would most likely foster resilience?
options: No feedback at all so that students do not rely on adults
Public comparison with classmates who made fewer errors
Praise focused on natural talent, such as "You are a natural at this"
Praise focused on strategies and effort, such as "You tried three approaches before finding one that worked"
questions.rationale: Process praise supports a growth mindset and willingness to take on challenges.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to promote deep processing during a lesson on the water cycle. Which task best achieves this?
options: Have students underline vocabulary words in the textbook
Have students recopy the definitions three times
Have students read the chapter silently once and answer a recall question
Have students create a labeled diagram and explain to a partner how each step causes the next
questions.rationale: Explaining relationships requires elaboration, a form of deep processing.

questions.stem: A teacher uses real objects, pictures, and short stories to introduce the concept of fractions to second graders. Which principle supports this approach?
options: Young learners learn best through abstract symbols presented first
Young learners rely mainly on lecture for new ideas
Young learners build abstract concepts from concrete, multi-sensory experiences
Young learners should avoid objects to prevent confusion
questions.rationale: Concrete experiences ground abstract ideas.

questions.stem: A teacher is aware that stress can affect memory. Which action is most likely to help students perform better on a stressful test?
options: Teach relaxation strategies and give low-stakes practice under similar conditions
Tell students that the test is the most important event of their lives
Increase the penalty for mistakes
Remove all breaks from the schedule
questions.rationale: Reducing anxiety frees working memory.

questions.stem: Why does a teacher give directions in short, numbered steps for a first-grade task?
options: Young children can hold ten steps in mind at once
Numbered steps replace the need for modeling
Numbered steps are mainly for older students
Young children have limited working memory capacity and benefit from small chunks
questions.rationale: Chunking directions respects working memory limits.

questions.stem: Which activity best supports the development of fine motor skills in a preschool classroom?
options: Memorizing a list of vocabulary words
Watching a video about drawing
Listening to a long story without movement
Stringing beads, using tweezers to move small objects, and tracing shapes
questions.rationale: Hands-on manipulation develops small-muscle control.

questions.stem: A middle school teacher notices that students who are beginning puberty at different times show differences in confidence and participation. Which instructional response is most developmentally appropriate?
options: Group students strictly by physical appearance
Create a supportive climate, provide choices, and avoid comparisons based on physical development
Ignore the differences and require identical participation
Make comments about students' changing appearance
questions.rationale: Early adolescents are sensitive to physical change and peer comparison.

questions.stem: A student who learned that "bat" refers to a flying animal now reads a passage about baseball and is confused by "bat." Which skill would best help the student?
options: Using context clues to decide which meaning of a multiple-meaning word fits
Memorizing a list of homophones
Ignoring unfamiliar words
Skipping the passage
questions.rationale: Context clues help determine the intended meaning.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to support a student who is in the speech emergence stage of English acquisition. Which task is most appropriate?
options: Ask the student to retell part of a story using a picture sequence and sentence starters
Ask the student to give a five-minute speech without notes
Assign advanced grammar exercises with no support
Have the student remain silent until fully fluent
questions.rationale: Speech emergence learners produce short phrases and sentences with support.

questions.stem: A student who is an emergent bilingual is in the silent period during the first weeks in class. What is the best response?
options: Provide comprehensible input and allow nonverbal responses while inviting participation
Assume the student has a speech disorder
Remove the student from class
Require the student to speak in front of the class
questions.rationale: Silent periods are normal and input still builds language.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a student with dysgraphia the option to dictate responses to a scribe or use speech-to-text. This is intended to
options: Penalize the student for slow writing
Lower the content standard for the student
Remove the barrier of handwriting while assessing the student's knowledge
Replace all writing instruction
questions.rationale: Dictation provides access without changing what is measured.

questions.stem: A student with a speech or language impairment avoids oral presentations. Which support best promotes participation?
options: Require the student to present to the whole school immediately
Offer options such as a recorded presentation or presenting to a small group first
Mock the student's speech to build thick skin
Skip all oral tasks permanently without a plan
questions.rationale: Graduated options build confidence.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a graphic organizer and sentence frames for all students in an inclusive science class. A student with an IEP does not need additional modification. Which principle explains this practice?
options: Grade acceleration, which moves students to higher grades
Tracking, which separates students by ability
Behavior modification, which relies on tangible rewards
Universal Design for Learning, which builds in supports for everyone so that fewer individual adaptations are needed
questions.rationale: UDL reduces barriers proactively for all learners.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to know a student's interests and strengths before planning instruction. Which strategy is most helpful?
options: Review only last year's test scores
Assume interests from the student's background
Ask classmates to describe the student
Use an interest inventory and conversations to learn about the student
questions.rationale: Interest inventories provide direct information.

questions.stem: A student whose family follows a religion that prohibits celebrating certain holidays is asked to participate in a class party. What should the teacher do?
options: Require participation because it is a class activity
Respect the family's beliefs by offering an alternative activity without penalty
Publicly question the family's beliefs
Lower the student's grade for nonparticipation
questions.rationale: Teachers should respect religious practices and avoid singling students out.

questions.stem: A teacher uses sentence frames such as "I notice ___ because ___" for a science discussion. Who benefits most from this support?
options: Only students who have mastered the content
Students who are developing academic language, including English learners
No students because frames limit thinking
Only students in advanced classes
questions.rationale: Frames scaffold academic talk.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that a gifted student is performing below potential and hides abilities to avoid standing out. What is the best response?
options: Provide challenging work, a supportive peer group, and counseling resources to address social-emotional needs
Ignore the behavior
Punish the student for underperforming
Remove the student from gifted services
questions.rationale: Gifted students may underachieve for social reasons.

questions.stem: A student with a physical disability needs more time to move between classes. Which accommodation is most appropriate?
options: Require the student to run to class
Allow the student to leave early or use an accessible route
Penalize the student for tardiness
Exclude the student from some classes
questions.rationale: Access to facilities is a basic accommodation.

questions.stem: A student has a hearing aid that sometimes squeals. What should the teacher do?
options: Ignore the problem
Make a public announcement about the sound
Tell the student to remove the device
Check with the student discreetly and follow up with the audiologist or nurse as needed
questions.rationale: Discreet follow-up protects dignity.

questions.stem: A teacher is planning a lesson on the water cycle. Which objective is most appropriately aligned with a hands-on investigation?
options: Students will know about the water cycle
Students will understand water
Students will like science
Students will model evaporation and condensation and explain each stage using observations
questions.rationale: Aligned objectives are specific and observable.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to build vocabulary knowledge before a reading assignment. Which activity best prepares students?
options: Skip vocabulary because students can use a dictionary
Assign the whole list for homework without discussion
Preview key words with images and examples, and have students use them in discussion
Quiz students on the words before introducing them
questions.rationale: Previewing and using words builds knowledge.

questions.stem: A teacher plans a unit using the TEKS but discovers that a standard in the unit builds on a skill from the previous grade that students may not have mastered. What should she do?
options: Skip the standard
Assess prerequisite skills and build in targeted review before teaching the new standard
Teach only the review for the entire unit
Assume all students have the prerequisite skill
questions.rationale: Planning should account for prerequisite knowledge.

questions.stem: A teacher introduces a lesson by asking, "How many of you have ever wondered why the sky is blue?" Which part of the lesson does this represent?
options: Guided practice with feedback
Anticipatory set that engages students and introduces the topic
Summative assessment
Closure that summarizes the lesson
questions.rationale: An opening question hooks interest.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that students lose focus when lessons lack variety. Which planning strategy best addresses this?
options: Teach only by lecture
Repeat the same activity daily
Vary activities, such as brief direct instruction, partner talk, and hands-on practice, within the lesson
Remove all active tasks
questions.rationale: Variety sustains attention.

questions.stem: A teacher plans a performance task in which students design a budget for a class party. Which standards are most likely integrated?
options: Math standards on operations and financial literacy with ELA standards on communicating a plan
Only art standards on color
Only science standards on matter
Only physical education standards on movement
questions.rationale: Real-world tasks integrate subjects.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a unit pacing guide that allots three weeks to fractions, but students need more time on equivalent fractions. What should the teacher do?
options: Eliminate assessments
Skip equivalent fractions
Adjust pacing within the unit while ensuring essential standards are still addressed
Move on regardless of mastery
questions.rationale: Pacing is flexible when evidence indicates need.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to apply math in real contexts. Which task is most authentic?
options: Copy a formula from the board
Calculate the cost of materials to build a garden bed and compare prices from two stores
Complete twenty identical computation problems
Memorize the multiplication table with no application
questions.rationale: Authentic tasks reflect real-world use.

questions.stem: A teacher integrates a read-aloud with a science topic about habitats. Which benefit is most likely?
options: Students build vocabulary and knowledge simultaneously through content-rich text
Students avoid learning science vocabulary
Students become only listeners
Students no longer need hands-on activities
questions.rationale: Content-rich texts build knowledge and language.

questions.stem: A teacher designs a lesson on persuasive writing and wants students to analyze a model essay first. What is the main purpose of using a mentor text?
options: To discourage students from developing their own voice
To make students copy the model exactly
To show the features of strong writing so students can emulate them in their own work
To replace the need for any instruction
questions.rationale: Mentor texts illustrate craft.

questions.stem: A teacher plans formative checks in a unit but also wants a summative project that measures transfer. Which design is most coherent?
options: Use only a final multiple-choice test of recall
Assign the same practice problems for the final project
Use formative checks only and no final assessment
Use formative checks to guide instruction and a final project that requires applying concepts in a new context
questions.rationale: Coherent plans align formative and summative tasks with goals.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to confirm that a test measures the standards taught. She asks a colleague to review each item against the objectives. What type of validity evidence is she collecting?
options: Content validity evidence through expert review of alignment
Test-retest evidence through repeated administration
Inter-rater reliability evidence through scorer agreement
Predictive validity evidence through later performance
questions.rationale: Expert review of alignment supports content validity.

questions.stem: A teacher uses several short quizzes rather than one long test. Which benefit is most likely?
options: Lower validity of scores
Less information for planning
More frequent feedback and a more reliable picture of student progress
Reduced need for instruction
questions.rationale: Frequent short checks give timely data.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that on a reading assessment students with disabilities perform better when directions are read aloud. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: The assessment may measure decoding of directions as well as the target skill, so reading directions aloud may be an appropriate accommodation
The students do not need accommodations
The assessment should be discontinued
The students are cheating when directions are read aloud
questions.rationale: Directions can introduce construct-irrelevant barriers.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to gather evidence of student understanding during a lesson without interrupting the flow. Which method is best?
options: Circulate and listen to partner conversations while noting misconceptions
Wait until the end of the unit
Ask only the strongest students
Stop the lesson for a long quiz
questions.rationale: Listening provides real-time evidence.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to use data from a benchmark test to group students for instruction. Which practice is most appropriate?
options: Use skill-level results to form flexible groups and reassess after instruction
Group students permanently by total score
Group by behavior only
Ignore the data and group alphabetically
questions.rationale: Data-based grouping should be flexible.

questions.stem: A teacher compares students' scores on a fall and spring assessment and calculates each student's gain. What is the limitation of using simple gain scores?
options: Gains can be affected by measurement error and by where students started on the scale
Gain scores eliminate the need for context
Gain scores are always perfectly reliable
Gain scores measure only attendance
questions.rationale: Measurement error and ceiling effects can distort growth estimates.

questions.stem: A teacher wants parents to understand a child's test scores. Which explanation is most appropriate?
options: Avoid discussing the scores
Give the numbers without any explanation
Use technical terms only
Explain what the test measures, what the score means, and how it will be used to support the child
questions.rationale: Clear communication helps families.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a student's strongest piece of work and the student's reflection to show growth in a portfolio conference. What is the purpose of the reflection?
options: To avoid teacher input
To help students analyze their own progress and set goals
To rank students
To replace all grades
questions.rationale: Reflection builds self-assessment skills.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to ensure that all students can see instruction materials and move easily. Which arrangement consideration is most important?
options: Clear sightlines and wide pathways, including for students who use mobility aids
Placing furniture to fill every available inch
Using only decorative items
Facing all desks toward the back wall
questions.rationale: Accessible layouts support all learners.

questions.stem: A teacher gives students a survey about how safe and respected they feel in class and uses results to adjust practices. This shows
options: A way to avoid planning
A grade for the teacher
An unnecessary task
Responsiveness to student perceptions of the learning environment
questions.rationale: Student feedback informs climate improvement.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that students from certain groups rarely volunteer. Which strategy best improves equity of voice without singling students out?
options: Use structured protocols that give every student a turn, such as round-robin or written responses shared aloud
Call on the same students for every question
Wait for volunteers only
Ask students to identify their group before speaking
questions.rationale: Structured turns reduce participation gaps.

questions.stem: A student shares that she feels invisible in class. Which teacher action best builds connection?
options: Ignore the comment
Move her seat to the back
Tell her to speak up more
Learn about her interests, greet her individually, and create opportunities for her to contribute
questions.rationale: Personal connection builds belonging.

questions.stem: A teacher uses affirming language when correcting behavior, such as "I know you can do better" instead of "You're always disruptive." What is the effect?
options: It encourages misbehavior
It eliminates consequences
It separates behavior from identity and preserves the relationship
It lowers expectations
questions.rationale: Respectful language maintains dignity.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to build a classroom culture where mistakes are valued. Which practice is most effective?
options: Hide all errors from the class
Share her own mistakes, analyze errors as a class, and praise revision
Punish mistakes with lower grades
Avoid challenging tasks
questions.rationale: Normalizing errors supports risk taking.

questions.stem: A teacher is teaching students to line up quickly and quietly. Which sequence is most effective?
options: Tell students once and expect perfection
Explain the expectation, model it, practice it, and give feedback
Skip the practice to save time
Punish the slowest student
questions.rationale: Procedures are taught like academic skills.

questions.stem: A student frequently leaves his seat to sharpen pencils during instruction. Which proactive step is most effective?
options: Ban pencils
Provide a supply of sharpened pencils and a clear routine for when to sharpen
Ignore the behavior
Send the student to the office
questions.rationale: Removing the cause prevents the behavior.

questions.stem: A teacher implements a behavior plan that gives students points for following expectations. After several weeks the behavior improves but the teacher wants to reduce reliance on points. What should she do?
options: Stop teaching expectations
Increase points indefinitely
Gradually thin the reinforcement and increase intrinsic supports such as praise and responsibility
Remove all reinforcement suddenly
questions.rationale: Fading reinforcement supports maintenance.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to engage in a discussion without interrupting one another. Which tool is most effective?
options: A talking object or structured turn-taking protocol
A punishment for any interruption
A ban on speaking
No guidelines
questions.rationale: Protocols support respectful dialogue.

questions.stem: A teacher sees a student crying quietly at his desk. What is the most appropriate initial response?
options: Check in privately and calmly, offer support, and involve the counselor if needed
Announce the crying to the class
Tell the student to stop crying
Ignore the student
questions.rationale: Responding with care supports well-being.

questions.stem: A teacher notes that a student's disruptions occur mostly when tasks are too difficult. Which intervention best addresses the function of the behavior?
options: Increase punishment for disruptions
Remove the student from all difficult tasks permanently
Adjust task difficulty with scaffolds and teach the student to request help appropriately
Give more difficult tasks to prove capability
questions.rationale: Matching intervention to function reduces behavior.

questions.stem: A teacher decides to hold a brief class meeting to address recurring noise problems and ask students for solutions. Which management approach is this?
options: Punitive discipline
Authoritarian control
Permissive management
Collaborative problem solving that builds ownership
questions.rationale: Class meetings involve students in solutions.

questions.stem: A teacher gives students a few minutes to rehearse an answer with a partner before sharing with the class. What communication benefit does this provide?
options: Students avoid thinking
Teachers avoid listening
Students never make errors
Students clarify ideas and gain confidence before speaking publicly
questions.rationale: Rehearsal improves quality and confidence.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that her use of "um" and "you know" is frequent. Which step would best improve her verbal communication?
options: Speak faster
Record a lesson, identify patterns, and practice planned pauses
Avoid speaking to students
Ignore it
questions.rationale: Self-observation helps improve delivery.

questions.stem: A teacher asks a question that has several possible answers and invites students to explain their thinking. This is an example of
options: A recall question
A divergent question that encourages multiple perspectives
A rhetorical question
A closed question with one answer
questions.rationale: Divergent questions have multiple valid responses.

questions.stem: A teacher explains a complex process, then asks students to teach it back to a partner using their own words. How does this strategy improve learning?
options: It replaces assessment
It ensures that no student makes errors
It reduces the need for any explanation
Teaching others requires organizing and elaborating knowledge, which deepens understanding and reveals gaps
questions.rationale: Explaining to others is a powerful learning strategy.

questions.stem: A teacher is giving a presentation to a class and notices students are confused by technical vocabulary. What should she do?
options: End the lesson immediately
Pause, define the term with an example, and check for understanding
Speak louder
Continue without explanation
questions.rationale: Responding to confusion improves clarity.

questions.stem: A teacher greets a student in the hallway by name and asks about a recent soccer game. What is the effect on communication in the classroom?
options: It builds rapport that makes students more willing to communicate
It is unprofessional
It creates favoritism
It wastes instructional time
questions.rationale: Personal attention supports positive relationships.

questions.stem: A teacher asks students to predict what will happen when a magnet is placed near different materials, test each, and revise predictions. Which skill is being used?
options: Memorizing a list of facts
Following directions without thinking
Copying results from the board
Hypothesis testing and revising ideas based on evidence
questions.rationale: Predict-test-revise reflects scientific inquiry.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to evaluate competing solutions to a community problem. Which structure best supports this thinking?
options: A list of the teacher's preferred solution
A decision matrix in which students identify criteria and rate each solution
A coin flip
A single vote with no discussion
questions.rationale: Decision matrices make reasoning explicit.

questions.stem: A teacher has students write a claim, support it with evidence, and explain their reasoning. Which framework is this?
options: Know-Want-Learn
Anticipation-Reaction
Claim-Evidence-Reasoning
Think-Pair-Share
questions.rationale: CER structures scientific and argumentative writing.

questions.stem: A teacher asks students to explain how a model of the solar system is useful and where it is inaccurate. Which skill is being developed?
options: Ignoring evidence
Evaluating models and understanding their limitations
Memorizing planet names only
Rote recitation
questions.rationale: Critiquing models builds scientific thinking.

questions.stem: A teacher uses think-alouds to model how she evaluates the reliability of a website. What is the main purpose of the think-aloud?
options: To avoid teaching the criteria
To show that websites are always reliable
To make expert reasoning visible so students can learn the process
To save time
questions.rationale: Think-alouds reveal strategies.

questions.stem: A teacher encourages students to use strong passwords and to log out of shared devices. Which concept is she teaching?
options: Online safety and protecting personal information
File compression
Keyboarding speed
Graphic design
questions.rationale: Safe practices protect accounts.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a tool that automatically scores student responses and provides a dashboard of results. What is the most important step before relying on the data?
options: Ignore student work samples
Verify that the tool's scoring is valid and reliable for the skill being measured
Share the dashboard publicly
Assume automated scores are always accurate
questions.rationale: Tools should be validated.

questions.stem: A teacher gives students a choice of using a digital tool or paper to create a poster, provided both meet criteria. Which principle does this reflect?
options: Elimination of criteria
Mandatory technology use
Flexibility in how students demonstrate learning
Lowered standards
questions.rationale: Choice supports diverse needs.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to teach students to cite digital sources correctly. Which activity is most effective?
options: Ignore citations
Model citation formats and have students practice with sources from a real research task
Allow copying without credit
Tell students to figure it out
questions.rationale: Modeling and practice build skill.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a rubric to score a presentation and notices that students lose points mostly in the area of eye contact. Which action best uses this information?
options: Lower all scores
Teach and practice eye contact strategies and provide feedback before the next presentation
Remove eye contact from the rubric
Ignore the pattern
questions.rationale: Patterns in rubric data guide instruction.

questions.stem: A teacher records a class's results on each standard and notes that only 40 percent of students mastered the standard on inference. What is the best next step?
options: Assume the standard is not important
Reteach inference with modeling and new texts and reassess
Give the same test again
Move to the next unit
questions.rationale: Low mastery calls for reteaching.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to give feedback that fosters independence. Which approach is best?
options: Avoid feedback to encourage independence
Ask guiding questions that help students find and correct errors themselves
Tell students only the final grade
Fix every error for students
questions.rationale: Guiding questions foster self-regulation.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a quiz with five items on each of three standards. A student gets all items correct on two standards and none on the third. What does this suggest?
options: A specific skill gap in the third standard that needs targeted instruction
The student is not capable
The student cheated
The test is invalid
questions.rationale: Standard-level patterns reveal specific needs.

questions.stem: A teacher sends a positive note home about a student's improvement. What is the likely impact on the family relationship?
options: It reduces the need for conferences
It creates unrealistic expectations
It builds trust and makes families more receptive to future communication
It causes misunderstandings
questions.rationale: Positive contact builds partnerships.

questions.stem: A family does not respond to emails. Which approach is most likely to reach them?
options: Ask about preferred communication methods and try alternatives such as phone calls or text through approved platforms
Stop contacting them
Send more emails of the same type
Assume the family does not care
questions.rationale: Flexible communication increases reach.

questions.stem: A teacher invites families to share traditions during a cultural celebration week. What is the primary benefit?
options: It replaces core instruction
It singles out some students
It values family cultures and strengthens home-school connections
It requires all families to participate
questions.rationale: Inviting participation honors diversity.

questions.stem: A teacher uses feedback from an evaluator to set a goal of increasing student talk in lessons. Which method would best track progress?
options: Rely on a general feeling
Ask students to vote
Record the proportion of time students speak in several lessons and compare over time
Stop tracking
questions.rationale: Data provide objective evidence of change.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to extend her knowledge about teaching English learners. Which resource is most useful?
options: Professional organizations, workshops, and mentors with expertise in language development
A rumor from a colleague
An outdated manual
A single blog post with no evidence
questions.rationale: Credible resources support learning.

questions.stem: A teacher disagrees with her team about assessment practices but the team has chosen a common approach. Which response is most professional?
options: Refuse to participate
Complain to parents
Implement the agreed approach, contribute data, and raise concerns constructively at the next meeting
Sabotage the plan
questions.rationale: Professional teams commit to decisions while offering input.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to take a photo of students working in groups to share on the school's social media page. What should she do first?
options: Post with students' full names
Post from a personal account
Post immediately
Check that media release forms are on file and follow district guidelines
questions.rationale: Photo use requires consent and policy compliance.

questions.stem: A parent asks a teacher to provide a recommendation letter that includes information about a student's disciplinary history. What should the teacher do?
options: Follow school policy and obtain consent before including education record information
Share the entire file
Include all details without consent
Refuse to write any letters
questions.rationale: Education records require consent for disclosure.

questions.stem: A teacher is told by a student that the student's parent hits the student. The student begs the teacher not to tell. What does the law require?
options: The teacher should wait until the student agrees
The teacher should confront the parent
The teacher should tell only the principal
The teacher must report to DFPS or law enforcement within 48 hours regardless of the student's request
questions.rationale: Reporting is mandatory.

questions.stem: A teacher is chaperoning a field trip and is asked by a student to keep a medication secret from the school nurse. What should the teacher do?
options: Keep the secret
Tell the whole class
Give the medication
Follow the district policy and inform the nurse or administrator so the student's health and safety are protected
questions.rationale: Medication must be managed safely.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to sign a document attesting that testing procedures were followed even though a student received unauthorized help. What should the teacher do?
options: Alter the student's answers
Ignore the request
Decline to sign a false statement and report the irregularity to the testing coordinator
Sign it to avoid conflict
questions.rationale: Educators must not falsify records.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to use a short clip from a documentary to illustrate a concept in class. Which condition most supports that the use is permitted?
options: The clip is copied and distributed to all students
The clip is lawfully obtained, used in face-to-face instruction, and directly relates to the lesson objectives
The clip is posted publicly
The clip is shown for entertainment at the end of the day
questions.rationale: Instructional use in face-to-face teaching may be permitted.

questions.stem: A teacher's student teacher posts photos of students on a personal account. What should the teacher do?
options: Share the photos with others
Instruct the student teacher to remove the posts and review privacy and district policy
Like the post
Ignore it
questions.rationale: Educators must protect student privacy.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to help third graders remember the order of operations. Which approach best applies research on memory?
options: Have students read the rule aloud once and move on
Teach a meaningful strategy, practice it in varied problems over several days, and quiz students at spaced intervals
Tell students to stare at the rule until it feels familiar
Assign one long worksheet the night before the test
questions.rationale: Spaced, varied retrieval practice strengthens long-term memory.

questions.stem: A teenager sleeps only five hours a night and has trouble concentrating in first period. Which statement best connects development and learning?
options: Sleep has no effect on memory
Attention depends only on motivation
Teens need less sleep than younger children
Adolescents need more sleep than adults, and sleep loss impairs attention and memory consolidation
questions.rationale: Sleep supports memory consolidation and attention.

questions.stem: A child plays "school" with dolls, assigning roles and using rules she invents. According to Vygotsky, why is this play developmentally important?
options: It is useful only for entertainment
It shows that the child has not developed language
It is only a distraction from real learning
It creates a zone in which children act beyond their age by following rules and practicing self-regulation
questions.rationale: Vygotsky saw imaginative play as leading development.

questions.stem: A student can recall a vocabulary word on a quiz but cannot use it in a sentence a week later. Which explanation fits information processing theory?
options: Vocabulary cannot be stored
The student has lost sensory memory
The information was rehearsed shallowly and not encoded in meaningful long-term memory
Long-term memory has no storage capacity
questions.rationale: Shallow encoding leads to forgetting.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a student a hint instead of the answer so the student can still do most of the thinking. Which concept applies?
options: Scaffolding, which provides support that fades as the learner gains skill
Assimilation, which fits new information to a scheme without change
Extinction, which weakens a response
Punishment, which decreases behavior
questions.rationale: Scaffolding offers just enough help.

questions.stem: A student who is blind needs a graph for a math lesson. Which accommodation is most appropriate?
options: A color-coded graph with a legend
A tactile or raised-line graph with braille labels
A smaller version of the graph
A verbal instruction to imagine the graph
questions.rationale: Tactile materials give access to visual information.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that a student with a learning disability in reading is doing well in discussions but struggles with written tests. Which accommodation might help?
options: Allow oral responses or a reader for test items that are not measuring reading
Give additional homework
Lower the grade level of the content
Remove the student from tests
questions.rationale: Accommodations remove barriers unrelated to the construct.

questions.stem: A teacher pairs an English learner with a bilingual peer for a science activity. What is the best way to structure the pairing?
options: Give both students clear roles and ensure the English learner also practices speaking in English
Avoid pairing English learners with peers
Allow the peer to speak for the English learner
Have the peer do the activity alone
questions.rationale: Structured pairing supports both content and language.

questions.stem: A teacher reads that students in her class come from multiple cultural backgrounds with different views on collaboration and competition. How should she plan instruction?
options: Use only individual tasks to avoid conflict
Ignore cultural differences
Use only competitive tasks because they are fair
Use a mix of cooperative and individual tasks and observe how students respond, adjusting for comfort and learning
questions.rationale: Flexible structures honor diverse preferences.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to build understanding of how ecosystems work. Which assessment aligns best with an objective about explaining food webs?
options: Students construct a food web for a given habitat and explain what would happen if one species disappeared
Students list the names of five habitats
Students copy a food web from the book
Students match animal names to pictures
