questions.rationale: Explaining consequences shows understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher integrates technology into a unit on community helpers by having students interview a local worker by video call. What is the main instructional benefit?
options: Students avoid doing any work
Students will not need assessments
Students no longer need to read
Students connect classroom learning to real-world experiences and practice communication
questions.rationale: Authentic experiences deepen learning.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to use data from an end-of-year test to decide which students need summer support. Which additional step improves decision accuracy?
options: Combine test results with classroom performance and teacher observations
Use only the family's request
Use only attendance data
Use only the test score
questions.rationale: Multiple measures improve accuracy.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a reading comprehension test that includes passages about snow skiing, which many students in her south Texas class have never experienced. Which concern is most relevant?
options: Practicality of the test only
Reliability of scoring only
Background knowledge bias that may lower scores unrelated to reading skill
Face validity of the font
questions.rationale: Unfamiliar contexts can disadvantage students.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to track whether a student is meeting a reading fluency goal of 90 words correct per minute by spring. Which measurement is most appropriate?
options: A single end-of-year multiple-choice test
A vocabulary matching quiz
Repeated one-minute oral reading probes graphed against the goal
A spelling test
questions.rationale: Fluency is measured by timed oral reading.

questions.stem: A teacher greets each student with a handshake or wave as they enter. What is the main benefit of this routine?
options: It builds positive relationships and sets a welcoming tone for the day
It replaces academic planning
It is required by state law
It eliminates all behavior problems
questions.rationale: Welcoming routines foster belonging.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that students from lower-income families rarely volunteer for leadership roles. Which action best addresses equitable access?
options: Rotate leadership roles systematically and explicitly invite all students to participate
Select only students with high grades
Select leaders based on who volunteers first
Assign leadership roles to the same students every time
questions.rationale: Systematic rotation ensures equal opportunity.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to address a student's feelings of being excluded by classmates. Which activity best builds inclusion?
options: Structured cooperative tasks where each student has a role and success depends on all members
A seating chart that isolates the student
A competition with one winner
A lecture on friendship only
questions.rationale: Cooperative tasks create interdependence.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a visual timer during independent work so students can see how much time remains. What is the main benefit?
options: It increases noise
It replaces the need for directions
It helps students manage time and reduces anxiety about transitions
It ensures every student finishes
questions.rationale: Visual timers support self-management.

questions.stem: A teacher notices a pattern of off-task behavior right after lunch. Which proactive adjustment is most likely to help?
options: Add a punishment for being off task
Ignore the pattern
Start the afternoon with a short, engaging activity and a calming routine
Cancel afternoon instruction
questions.rationale: Planning for predictable times prevents problems.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to understand the reasons for classroom rules. Which approach best supports internalization?
options: Post rules without explanation
Enforce rules only when the principal visits
Discuss why each rule matters and connect it to a respectful, productive community
Change rules daily
questions.rationale: Understanding purpose supports internalization.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to clarify a misconception during a discussion. Which move best maintains student dignity?
options: Ignore the misconception
Restate the idea neutrally, ask a probing question, and guide students toward the correct reasoning
Tell the student the idea is stupid
Move on to another student without comment
questions.rationale: Respectful correction maintains safety.

questions.stem: A teacher writes the lesson objective on the board in student-friendly language and refers to it during the lesson. What is the benefit?
options: The teacher can skip planning
The objective replaces assessment
Students will learn without practice
Students stay focused on the purpose and can monitor their own progress
questions.rationale: Visible objectives clarify expectations.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a question sequence that begins with recall, moves to explanation, and ends with evaluation. What is the purpose of sequencing questions this way?
options: To avoid assessing recall
To limit student participation
To confuse students
To scaffold students toward higher-level thinking by building on foundational knowledge
questions.rationale: Sequenced questions build thinking.

questions.stem: A teacher asks students to read two articles with opposing views and decide which author provides stronger evidence. Which skill is targeted?
options: Recalling the title
Spelling accuracy
Handwriting speed
Evaluating arguments and evidence
questions.rationale: Comparing evidence requires evaluation.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to learn how to break a large project into smaller tasks. Which skill is being developed?
options: Planning and organizing complex tasks
Copying a plan
Memorizing steps
Rushing to finish
questions.rationale: Decomposing tasks is a planning skill.

questions.stem: A teacher uses an anchor chart that lists "What good problem solvers do": understand the problem, make a plan, carry it out, and look back. Which framework is this?
options: Polya's four-step problem-solving process
Maslow's hierarchy of needs
Skinner's operant model
Piaget's stages of development
questions.rationale: Polya outlined understanding, planning, carrying out, and reflecting.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to provide students with immediate feedback on a short quiz and give herself class-level data. Which technology is most suitable?
options: A digital quiz platform that scores responses automatically and shows results
A television show
A paper test returned next week
A slide deck with no questions
questions.rationale: Immediate digital feedback supports instruction.

questions.stem: A teacher creates a class website with assignments, links, and contact information. What is the primary benefit for families?
options: Elimination of all communication
Privacy for the teacher only
Easy access to expectations and resources
Replacement of conferences
questions.rationale: Websites increase transparency.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a pretest, teaches a unit, and gives a posttest using parallel items. What is the primary purpose of using parallel items?
options: To compare performance on equivalent content before and after instruction
To avoid grading
To reduce the need for any teaching
To rank students
questions.rationale: Parallel forms allow comparison of growth.

questions.stem: A teacher asks students to underline the part of their writing that best meets a rubric criterion and explain why. How does this help?
options: It eliminates the need for revision
It replaces teacher feedback
It develops students' ability to apply criteria to their own work
It lowers expectations
questions.rationale: Self-assessment with criteria builds skill.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to help families understand how their child's reading level is determined. Which approach is most effective?
options: Explain the assessment in plain language, share sample items, and describe how results guide instruction
Use technical terms only
Avoid the topic
Send a score report without explanation
questions.rationale: Clear explanations help families participate.

questions.stem: A teacher learns that a family's work schedule prevents attendance at school events. Which response best supports partnership?
options: Require attendance at every event
Offer alternatives such as recorded messages, online meetings, or flexible conference times
Stop communicating
Penalize the family for not attending
questions.rationale: Flexibility supports engagement.

questions.stem: A teacher engages in action research by testing a new writing routine in one class and comparing results to another class. Which element is most important for a fair comparison?
options: Similar students and consistent measurement of outcomes in both classes
Using different tests for each class
Ignoring data
Choosing the class that will look better
questions.rationale: Fair comparison requires comparable groups and measures.

questions.stem: A teacher learns that a student's parents are divorcing and a custody order limits one parent's access to the student. A parent asks to pick up the student. What should the teacher do?
options: Release the student to any parent who asks
Ignore the custody order
Follow the school's pickup procedures and check with administration regarding the custody order
Ask the student to decide
questions.rationale: Schools must follow valid court orders.

questions.stem: A parent who does not have custody asks for the student's grades. What does FERPA generally say?
options: Neither parent may see records
Only the student may see records
Only the custodial parent may ever see records
Either parent generally has access to education records unless a court order or law specifically revokes the right
questions.rationale: FERPA gives rights to both parents absent a court order.

questions.stem: A teacher is serving on a hiring committee and the candidate is a close relative. What is the most ethical action?
options: Disclose the relationship and recuse from the decision
Vote for the relative
Keep the relationship secret
Lobby the other members
questions.rationale: Conflicts of interest must be disclosed.

questions.stem: A coach wants to give an athlete extra time off class for practice and promises a better grade in exchange for effort. Which concern is most relevant?
options: Grades must reflect academic achievement, not athletic participation
Practice is illegal
The coach cannot talk to students
Athletes cannot have any extra time
questions.rationale: Grading integrity is an ethical requirement.

questions.stem: A district policy requires teachers to report any suspected violation of the Educators' Code of Ethics by a colleague. A teacher hears a rumor that a coworker plans to leave a test booklet unlocked. What is the best action?
options: Confront the coworker publicly
Report the concern to the testing coordinator or administrator so the issue can be investigated
Spread the rumor to others
Ignore the rumor
questions.rationale: Reporting protects test security.

questions.stem: A student with a documented disability asks for extra time on a project. The teacher believes the student is just procrastinating. What should the teacher do?
options: Deny the request without checking
Review the student's plan and provide the documented accommodation
Tell the student to find another class
Penalize the student for asking
questions.rationale: Documented accommodations must be provided.

questions.stem: A teacher notices a student who frequently falls asleep in class and seems hungry. Which action best supports the student?
options: Embarrass the student publicly
Ignore the student
Check in privately and connect the student with the counselor and resources such as school meal programs
Punish the student for sleeping
questions.rationale: Basic needs affect learning.

questions.stem: A teacher is creating an assessment that includes both multiple-choice items and a short performance task. What is the advantage of mixing item types?
options: It makes scoring unnecessary
It guarantees higher scores
Different formats capture different kinds of knowledge and provide a fuller picture of learning
It reduces validity
questions.rationale: Multiple formats broaden evidence.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to teach a lesson on the causes of the Civil War using multiple perspectives. Which resource set best supports this goal?
options: Primary sources from Northern and Southern viewpoints along with a secondary summary
Only videos with no text
A single political speech
Only a one-sided textbook paragraph
questions.rationale: Multiple perspectives build historical thinking.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a green-yellow-red noise meter during group work. What is the main purpose?
options: To give students visual feedback so they can regulate their volume
To replace group work
To stop all talking
To punish talkative students
questions.rationale: Visual feedback supports self-regulation.

questions.stem: A teacher gives students a mystery object and asks them to ask yes-or-no questions to figure out what it is. Which skill is being developed?
options: Questioning and reasoning by narrowing possibilities
Following directions only
Copying peers
Memorizing facts
questions.rationale: Strategic questioning develops reasoning.

questions.stem: A teacher uses closed captions in videos for the whole class. Which students benefit?
options: Only advanced readers
English learners, students with hearing loss, and students who benefit from reading along
No students
Only students with hearing loss
questions.rationale: Captions support many learners.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that giving more detailed feedback increased student revisions but students still repeat the same errors. What should the teacher do next?
options: Stop giving feedback
Teach the skill explicitly with modeling and practice, then reassess to see whether errors decrease
Lower expectations
Give even longer comments
questions.rationale: Feedback alone may not teach missing skills.

questions.stem: A teacher offers parents a short guide with questions to ask their child about school each day. What is the benefit?
options: It requires parents to teach the curriculum
It replaces teacher communication
It gives families practical ways to engage in conversations about learning
It reduces student responsibility
questions.rationale: Simple tools support engagement.

questions.stem: A teacher gives students a graphic organizer to plan what they will say in a presentation. What communication skill does this support?
options: Memorizing a script
Avoiding eye contact
Speaking quickly
Organizing ideas before speaking
questions.rationale: Planning improves clarity.

questions.stem: A teacher explains that students with a strong sense of belonging in school tend to persist longer on hard tasks. Which need from self-determination theory does this illustrate?
options: Safety, the need for physical security only
Competence, the need to feel capable on tasks
Autonomy, the need to have choice and control
Relatedness, the need to feel connected to others
questions.rationale: Self-determination theory identifies autonomy, competence, and relatedness as basic needs.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a student a choice of topics, shows how the work connects to the student's goals, and provides feedback on progress. Which motivational strategy is this?
options: Comparing students publicly
Supporting autonomy, relevance, and competence to foster intrinsic motivation
Giving tangible rewards for every task
Using punishment to increase effort
questions.rationale: Choice, relevance, and feedback support intrinsic motivation.

questions.stem: A student writes a sentence backwards and a teacher wonders about a developmental delay. Which observation would best indicate whether this is typical?
options: Whether the student is a young child still learning directionality, since reversals are common in early writing
Whether the student likes to read
Whether the student has siblings
Whether the student is tall for the grade
questions.rationale: Letter and word reversals are common in early writing.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a Venn diagram to compare two cultures' holiday traditions, inviting students to describe their own. Which outcome is most likely?
options: Students learn that only one tradition is correct
Students see similarities and differences and feel their backgrounds are valued
Students avoid discussing family
Students feel pressured to represent their entire culture
questions.rationale: Comparing traditions with choice builds understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to differentiate instruction in a heterogeneous class but has limited time. Which practice provides the greatest efficiency?
options: Use pre-assessment data to form flexible groups and tiered tasks for key lessons
Eliminate differentiation entirely
Teach to the middle only
Create a separate lesson plan for every student every day
questions.rationale: Targeted differentiation based on data is efficient.

questions.stem: A teacher wants students to understand the concept of symmetry. Which sequence best follows effective instruction?
options: Skip exploration and give notes only
Assign a test before any activity
Explore with folding paper, name the concept, and then apply it to new shapes
Give the definition and a quiz immediately
questions.rationale: Concrete exploration followed by naming and application deepens understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a unit planner that lists essential vocabulary, key questions, assessments, and activities for each week. What is the main advantage?
options: Less student engagement
Elimination of assessments
No need for daily planning
Coherence and alignment across the unit
questions.rationale: Unit planning aligns components.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to measure students' ability to solve multi-step problems. Which scoring approach is most informative?
options: A grade based on speed
A single point for the final answer only
A rubric that awards points for setup, process, and accuracy
A grade based on neatness
questions.rationale: Partial credit by criteria shows understanding.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a reading inventory to place students in groups. Which statement about this use is accurate?
options: Inventory results make groups permanent
Inventory results are not useful for planning
Inventory results replace all other data
Inventory results should be one source of information and groups should change as students grow
questions.rationale: Flexible grouping responds to new data.

questions.stem: A teacher greets a student who is learning English with a few words in the student's home language. What is the primary effect?
options: It prevents the student from learning English
It reduces the teacher's authority
It is considered unprofessional
It signals respect and helps the student feel welcome
questions.rationale: Valuing home language fosters belonging.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that classroom jokes about stereotypes make some students uncomfortable. Which response is most effective for climate?
options: Ignore it because it is just humor
Calmly address the impact, restate respectful norms, and teach how stereotypes cause harm
Punish the whole class
Laugh to avoid embarrassment
questions.rationale: Addressing the impact builds understanding.

questions.stem: A student takes materials from a classmate without asking. Which response best teaches responsibility?
options: Have the student return the item, apologize, and practice asking for what is needed
Publicly shame the student
Ignore the behavior
Send the student home without discussion
questions.rationale: Restitution and skill teaching build responsibility.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a clear one-sentence reminder of expectations before a group activity. What is the benefit?
options: Students will never need reminders
Students stop thinking
Students know the behavioral expectations and are more likely to meet them
Group work becomes unnecessary
questions.rationale: Brief reminders prompt appropriate behavior.

questions.stem: A teacher presents a chart where two variables rise together and asks students whether one causes the other. Which concept should students consider?
options: Charts cannot show relationships
Correlation is the same as proof
Correlation does not by itself prove causation, so other explanations must be examined
Any two rising variables are causally related
questions.rationale: Critical thinkers distinguish correlation from causation.

questions.stem: A teacher asks students to explain why different measurements of the same object might vary slightly. Which skill is targeted?
options: Understanding sources of error and uncertainty in data
Ignoring variation
Copying measurements
Memorizing units only
questions.rationale: Reasoning about error supports scientific thinking.

questions.stem: A teacher uses an interactive whiteboard to annotate a text while students follow on their devices. Which benefit is most likely?
options: Reduced student engagement
Less need for planning
Shared visual focus and real-time modeling of reading strategies
Elimination of discussion
questions.rationale: Annotation models strategies visibly.

questions.stem: A teacher considers using a generative AI tool to help students draft ideas. Which practice best protects learning and integrity?
options: Allow unrestricted use with no explanation
Set clear guidelines for appropriate use, require students to show their own thinking and cite assistance, and verify accuracy
Accept all output as accurate
Ban students from ever seeing the tool
questions.rationale: Clear guidelines and verification maintain integrity.

questions.stem: A teacher holds a short conference with each student about a recent assessment, asking the student to identify one strength and one goal. What does this practice develop?
options: Dependence on the teacher
Student ownership of learning and goal-setting skills
Avoidance of feedback
A reduction in learning time
questions.rationale: Conferences support reflection.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to know whether a student's improvement on a quiz is due to learning or luck. Which step helps most?
options: Stop collecting data
Collect additional evidence on the same skill using different tasks
Assume the improvement is real
Assume the improvement is luck
questions.rationale: Multiple pieces of evidence improve confidence.

questions.stem: A teacher notices that a parent is hesitant to share concerns during a conference. Which strategy best invites dialogue?
options: Avoid asking for input
Dominate the conversation
Rush through the agenda
Ask open-ended questions, listen actively, and thank the parent for sharing
questions.rationale: Open questions invite participation.

questions.stem: A teacher sets a goal to increase positive feedback to students and asks a colleague to observe. Which observation tool would be most useful?
options: A count of how many students were present
A list of the teacher's favorite students
A general impression of the teacher's mood
A tally of positive and corrective comments by type during a lesson
questions.rationale: Tallies provide objective data on feedback.

questions.stem: A teacher is asked to supervise a student on the playground during recess but is called away by a phone call. What is the best action?
options: Take the call and ignore the playground
Arrange for another adult to supervise before leaving
Leave the students alone briefly
Ask a student to watch the others
questions.rationale: Supervision must be continuous.

questions.stem: A teacher shares with a colleague that a student has a disability in a crowded faculty lounge where other staff and a visitor can overhear. Which responsibility has been breached?
options: Providing equal access
Following copyright law
Maintaining confidentiality of student information in appropriate settings
Meeting accessibility requirements
questions.rationale: Confidential information must be discussed privately.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to take students to a religious site for a social studies lesson. Which approach complies with the Establishment Clause?
options: Penalize students who decline to participate in rituals
Visit for educational purposes with no required participation in religious practices
Promote one religion
Require students to pray
questions.rationale: Educational visits are allowed if not promoting religion.

questions.stem: A teacher is aware of a new policy that requires reporting any student statements about harming themselves. A student says in a journal entry that life is not worth living. What should the teacher do?
options: Wait to see whether more entries appear
Follow the protocol and notify the counselor or administrator right away
Tell classmates to check on the student
Return the journal without comment
questions.rationale: Suicide risk requires immediate action.

questions.stem: A teacher uses a graphic organizer with pictures to teach a science concept to a student with an intellectual disability. What is the main purpose?
options: To replace the IEP
To reduce all academic expectations without a plan
To make abstract ideas more concrete and accessible while keeping the learning goal appropriate to the IEP
To keep the student from participating
questions.rationale: Visual supports increase access.

questions.stem: A teacher gives a pretest, midpoint check, and posttest in a unit. Which comparison best shows the effect of instruction?
options: Comparing the length of tests
Comparing the number of absent students
Comparing students to the teacher's favorite student
Comparing growth from pretest to posttest on the same skills
questions.rationale: Growth across measures shows instructional effect.

questions.stem: A teacher implements a classroom economy where students earn money for responsibilities and spend it on privileges. Which concern should the teacher consider?
options: Rewards never affect motivation
Extrinsic rewards can undermine intrinsic motivation if overused and may disadvantage students who earn less
Money cannot be used in classrooms
Rewards are illegal
questions.rationale: Overjustification can reduce intrinsic interest.

questions.stem: A teacher participates in a learning walk where colleagues visit classrooms to look for evidence of student engagement and then discuss patterns without evaluating individuals. What is the purpose?
options: To punish low engagement
To determine which teacher to dismiss
To identify schoolwide trends and learn from each other without judgment of individuals
To grade the teacher
questions.rationale: Learning walks focus on shared learning.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to share a student's strengths and needs with a family that has limited English. Which resource best ensures accurate understanding?
options: A note in English only
A qualified interpreter and a translated summary
An online translation of the full report with no review
A child translating for the parent
questions.rationale: Professional interpreters ensure accuracy.

questions.stem: A teacher uses the "I do, we do, you do" language during a lesson. What is the communication purpose of using consistent phrases?
options: To confuse students
To signal to students the level of support and what is expected at each phase
To end the lesson
To avoid modeling
questions.rationale: Consistent language clarifies roles.
